title.zh: 卷一百八十五 志第一百三十八 食貨下七
title.raw: 卷一百八十五 志第一百三十八 食貨下七 Volume 185 Treatises 138: Finance and Economics 2g

sentences.zh: 食貨下七○酒坑冶礬香附

translations.literal: Food and Goods, Part Seven ○ Wine, Mining Pits, Smelting, Alum, and Fragrant Herbs
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics 7 — Wine Monopoly, Mines, Smelting, Alum, and Incense

sentences.zh: 酒宋榷酤之法：諸州城內皆置務釀酒，縣、鎮、鄉、閭或許民釀而定其歲課，若有遺利，所在多請官酤。

translations.literal: Wine — Song monopoly-brewing law: in every prefectural city within the walls they established offices to brew wine; in counties, market-towns, villages, and hamlets they sometimes permitted the people to brew and set an annual quota; if surplus profit remained, in many places they requested government monopoly sales.
translations.idiomatic: Wine. Under the Song monopoly on intoxicants, every prefectural seat had government brewing offices; in counties, towns, villages, and hamlets private brewing might be allowed subject to a fixed annual levy, but wherever untapped revenue remained local authorities usually petitioned for state monopoly sales.

sentences.zh: 三京官造曲，聽民納直以取。

translations.literal: In the three capitals the government manufactured yeast-cakes; the people were permitted to pay cash to obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: In the three metropolitan capitals the state produced distiller's yeast, which private brewers could purchase for cash.

sentences.zh: 陳、滑、蔡、潁、隨、郢、鄧、金、房州、信陽軍舊皆不榷。

translations.literal: Chen, Hua, Cai, Ying, Sui, Ying, Deng, Jin, and Fang prefectures and Xinyang Military Prefecture formerly were all without monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, Hua, Cai, Ying, Sui, Ying [Jingzhou], Deng, Jin, Fang prefectures and Xinyang Military District had long been exempt from the monopoly.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，京西轉運使程能請榷之，所在置官吏局署，取民租米麥給釀，以官錢市薪槱及吏工奉料。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, Jingxi transport commissioner Cheng Neng requested to monopolize them; everywhere they set up official bureaus with clerks, took the people's tax grain of rice and wheat to supply brewing, and used government money to buy firewood and fuel and pay clerk and worker salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era (976–984), Jingxi transport commissioner Cheng Neng petitioned to bring these regions under monopoly control. Officials were posted to bureaus everywhere; tenant grain in rice and wheat was requisitioned for brewing, and government funds covered fuel and staff wages.

sentences.zh: 歲計獲無幾，而主吏規其盈羨，及醞齊不良，酒多醨薄，至課民婚葬，量戶大小令酤，民甚被其害。

translations.literal: Annual reckonings yielded little, yet chief clerks schemed for surplus; moreover brewing was poorly done, wine was mostly sour and thin, until they assessed the people's weddings and funerals and according to household size ordered them to buy — the people were greatly harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Annual returns proved meager, yet supervising clerks still chased paper surpluses; fermentation was poor and the wine often thin and sour. Households were assessed by size and compelled to purchase for weddings and funerals, to the people's great distress.

sentences.zh: 歲儉物貴，殆不償其費。

translations.literal: In years of scarcity goods were costly; they scarcely recovered their expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years, when prices were high, the operation barely covered its costs.

sentences.zh: 太宗知其弊，淳化五年，詔募民自釀，輸官錢減常課三之二，使其易辦；

translations.literal: Taizong knew its abuses; in Chunhua year 5 he decreed to recruit the people to brew themselves, paying government money with the regular levy reduced by two-thirds, to make it easier to manage;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong recognized these abuses. In 994 (Chunhua 5) he ordered private brewing under license, with the statutory payment to the state cut by two-thirds to ease compliance.

sentences.zh: 民有應募者，檢視其資產，長吏及大姓共保之，後課不登則均償。

translations.literal: When the people responded to the recruitment, their assets were inspected; district magistrates and great clans jointly guaranteed them; if later the levy was not fulfilled they would share compensation equally.
translations.idiomatic: Applicants had their assets reviewed; local magistrates and leading families stood as joint guarantors, with shared liability if quotas later went unmet.

sentences.zh: 是歲，取諸州歲課錢少者四百七十二處，募民自酤，或官賣曲收其直。

translations.literal: That year, at four hundred seventy-two places where the annual levies of the various prefectures were small, they recruited the people to brew and sell themselves, or the government sold yeast-cakes and collected the price.
translations.idiomatic: That year, at 472 low-yield districts, licensed private sale was introduced; elsewhere the state sold yeast and collected payment directly.

sentences.zh: 其後民應募者寡，猶多官釀。

translations.literal: Afterward few people responded to the recruitment; government brewing still predominated.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward few people took up the licenses, and government brewing still predominated.

sentences.zh: 陝西雖榷酤，而尚多遺利。

translations.literal: Shaanxi, though under monopoly brewing, still had much surplus profit untapped.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was under the monopoly, yet much revenue still went uncaptured.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，度支員外郎李士衡請增課以助邊費，乃歲增十一萬餘貫。

translations.literal: In Xianping year 5, Revenue Bureau vice commissioner Li Shiheng requested to increase the levy to assist frontier expenses; the annual increase was thus more than one hundred ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002 (Xianping 5), Revenue Bureau vice commissioner Li Shiheng petitioned to raise levies to help frontier costs, adding more than 110,000 strings of cash per year.

sentences.zh: 兩浙舊募民掌榷，雍熙初，以民多私釀，遂蠲其禁，其榷酤歲課如曲錢之制，附兩稅均率。

translations.literal: The Two Zhe circuits formerly recruited the people to manage the monopoly; at the beginning of Yongxi, because the people brewed much in secret, they abolished the prohibition; the annual monopoly levy followed the yeast-money system and was apportioned with the two tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Zhe circuits had once licensed private operators to run the monopoly. Early in the Yongxi era (984–987), widespread illicit brewing led to lifting the ban; the wine levy was then folded into the two-tax rolls like the yeast fee.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔曰：「有司請罷杭州榷酤，乃使豪舉之家坐專其利，貧弱之戶歲責所輸，本欲惠民，乃成侵擾。

translations.literal: In year 2 an edict said: "The authorities requested to abolish Hangzhou monopoly brewing, which allowed powerful families to sit and monopolize the profit while poor and weak households were annually assessed what they owed; the intent was to benefit the people, yet it became harassment."
translations.idiomatic: In 985 an edict declared: "When officials proposed ending Hangzhou's wine monopoly, wealthy clans seized the trade while poor households still paid annual assessments. A measure meant to help the people became harassment instead."

sentences.zh: 宜仍舊榷酒，罷納所均錢。

translations.literal: It is fitting to continue the old monopoly on wine and abolish payment of the apportioned money.
translations.idiomatic: The monopoly on wine should be restored and the apportioned levy abolished.

sentences.zh: 」天禧四年，轉運副使方仲荀言：「本道酒課舊額十四萬貫，遺利尚多。

translations.literal: " In Tianxi year 4, transport vice commissioner Fang Zhongxun said: "This circuit's wine levy old quota is one hundred forty thousand strings; surplus profit still remains considerable."
translations.idiomatic: " In 1020 (Tianxi 4), transport vice commissioner Fang Zhongxun reported: "This circuit's wine quota stands at 140,000 strings, yet considerable revenue remains untapped."

sentences.zh: 」乃歲增課九萬八千貫。

translations.literal: " The annual levy was thus increased by ninety-eight thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: " The annual levy was raised by 98,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 川峽承舊制，賣曲價重，開寶二年，詔減十之二。

translations.literal: The Sichuan gorges followed the old system; the price of sold yeast-cakes was heavy; in Kaibao year 2 an edict reduced it by two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan followed the old system, with yeast prices set high. In 969 (Kaibao 2) an edict cut the price by one-fifth.

sentences.zh: 既而頗興榷酤，言事者多陳其非便，太平興國七年罷，仍舊賣曲。

translations.literal: Soon afterward monopoly brewing was widely instituted; memorialists often stated its inconvenience; in Taiping Xingguo year 7 it was abolished, and selling yeast-cakes continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly brewing was soon extended widely, but memorialists repeatedly protested its drawbacks. In 982 (Taiping Xingguo 7) the monopoly was withdrawn and yeast sales resumed under the old rules.

sentences.zh: 自是，惟夔、達、開、施、瀘、黔、涪、黎、威州、梁山雲安軍，及河東之麟、府州，荊湖之辰州，福建之福、泉、汀、漳州、興化軍，廣南東、西路不禁。

translations.literal: From then on, only Kui, Da, Kai, Shi, Lu, Qian, Fu, Li, Wei prefectures, Liangshan and Yun'an Military Prefectures, and in Hedong Lin and Fu prefectures, in Jing-Hu Chen prefecture, in Fujian Fu, Quan, Ting, Zhang prefectures and Xinghua Military Prefecture, and the Eastern and Western Routes of Guangnan were without prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter only Kui, Da, Kai, Shi, Lu, Qian, Fu, Li, Wei, Liangshan, Yun'an, Hedong's Lin and Fu, Jing-Hu's Chen, Fujian's Fu, Quan, Ting, Zhang and Xinghua, and all of Guangnan East and West remained exempt from the monopoly.

sentences.zh: 自春至秋，醞成即鬻，謂之「小酒」，其價自五錢至三十錢，有二十六等；

translations.literal: From spring to autumn, when brewing was finished it was sold at once — called "small wine"; its price ranged from five cash to thirty cash, with twenty-six grades;
translations.idiomatic: From spring through autumn, wine was sold as soon as fermentation finished — called "small wine," priced from 5 to 30 cash in twenty-six grades;

sentences.zh: 臘釀蒸鬻，候夏而出，謂之「大酒」，自八錢至四十八錢，有二十三等。

translations.literal: Brewed in the twelfth month and steamed for sale, released when summer came — called "large wine"; from eight cash to forty-eight cash, with twenty-three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brews were steamed and held until summer — called "large wine," from 8 to 48 cash in twenty-three grades.

sentences.zh: 凡醞用粳、糯、粟、黍、麥等及曲法、酒式，皆從水土所宜。

translations.literal: For all brewing, use of japonica, glutinous, millet, broomcorn, wheat and the like, and yeast methods and wine types, all followed what local soil and water suited.
translations.idiomatic: Grains used — japonica, glutinous rice, millet, broomcorn, wheat, and so on — together with yeast recipes and wine styles, all followed local soil and water conditions.

sentences.zh: 諸州官釀所費穀麥，準常糴以給，不得用倉儲。

translations.literal: Grain and wheat expended by official brewing in the various prefectures was supplied according to regular purchase prices; they might not use granary stores.
translations.idiomatic: Grain for official brewing in the prefectures had to be bought at regular market rates; granary stocks could not be used.

sentences.zh: 酒匠、役人當受糧者給錢。

translations.literal: Brewing craftsmen and corvée laborers who should receive grain were given money instead.
translations.idiomatic: Brewers and corvée workers who would normally receive grain rations were paid in cash.

sentences.zh: 凡官曲，麥一斗為曲六斤四兩。

translations.literal: For all official yeast-cakes, one dou of wheat made six jin four liang of yeast.
translations.idiomatic: Official yeast was made at the rate of one dou of wheat to six jin four liang of yeast.

sentences.zh: 賣曲價：東京、南京斤直錢百五十五，西京減五。

translations.literal: Price for selling yeast: Eastern Capital and Southern Capital, per jin straight price one hundred fifty-five cash; Western Capital reduced by five.
translations.idiomatic: Yeast prices: 155 cash per jin in the Eastern and Southern Capitals, 150 in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 咸平末，江、淮製置增榷酤錢，頗為煩刻。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianping, Jiang-Huai commissioners increased monopoly-brewing money, which was quite troublesome and exacting.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xianping era, Jiang-Huai commissioners raised monopoly revenues in ways that proved burdensome and exacting.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，詔毋增榷，自後製置使不得兼領酒榷。

translations.literal: In Jingde year 2 an edict forbade increasing the monopoly; thereafter commissioners might not concurrently head the wine monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005 (Jingde 2) an edict barred further monopoly increases; commissioners were thereafter forbidden to oversee the wine monopoly concurrently.

sentences.zh: 四年，又詔中外不得更議增課以圖恩獎。

translations.literal: In year 4 another edict said that inside and outside the court they must not again discuss increasing levies to seek favor and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1007 another edict forbade officials at court and in the provinces from proposing levy increases to win favor and rewards.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，著作郎張師德使淮南，上言：「鄉村酒戶年額少者，望並停廢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, Academician Zhang Shide was envoy to Huainan and memorialized: "Village wine households with small annual quotas — it is hoped they may all be stopped and abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxi era, Academician Zhang Shide, on mission to Huainan, proposed abolishing rural wine franchises with low annual quotas.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，兩京諸州收榷課銅錢一百二十一萬四千餘貫、鐵錢一是五十六萬五千餘貫，京城賣曲錢四十八萬餘貫。

translations.literal: In Zhidao year 2, the two capitals and various prefectures collected monopoly levies in copper cash of one million two hundred fourteen thousand plus strings, iron cash of one [hundred?] five hundred sixty-five thousand plus strings, and capital-city yeast sales of four hundred eighty thousand plus strings.
translations.idiomatic: In 996 (Zhidao 2), the two capitals and prefectures collected monopoly revenues of 1,214,000+ strings in copper cash, about 1,565,000 strings in iron cash, and 480,000+ strings from yeast sales in the capital.

sentences.zh: 天禧末，榷課銅錢增七百七十九萬六千餘貫，鐵錢增一百三十五萬四千餘貫，曲錢增三十九萬一千餘貫。

translations.literal: By the end of Tianxi, monopoly levies in copper cash increased by seven million seven hundred ninety-six thousand plus strings, iron cash increased by one million three hundred fifty-four thousand plus strings, yeast money increased by three hundred ninety-one thousand plus strings.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Tianxi era, monopoly revenues had risen by 7,796,000 strings in copper cash, 1,354,000 in iron cash, and 391,000 from yeast sales.

sentences.zh: 五代漢初，犯私曲者並棄市；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Han in the Five Dynasties, those who violated private yeast-cakes were all executed in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han of the Five Dynasties, illicit yeast production was punished by public execution;

sentences.zh: 周，至五斤者死。

translations.literal: Under Zhou, up to five jin meant death.
translations.idiomatic: under the Later Zhou, amounts up to five jin carried the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，以周法太峻，犯私曲至十五斤、以私酒入城至三斗者始處極刑，餘論罪有差；

translations.literal: In Jianlong year 2, because Zhou law was too severe, only private yeast up to fifteen jin and bringing private wine into the city up to three dou received the extreme penalty; for the rest crimes were graded;
translations.idiomatic: In 961 (Jianlong 2), finding Zhou penalties too harsh, capital punishment was limited to fifteen jin of illicit yeast or three dou of illicit wine brought into cities; lesser amounts received graded sentences;

sentences.zh: 私市酒、曲者減造人罪之半。

translations.literal: Those who privately marketed wine or yeast had their crime reduced by half compared to makers.
translations.idiomatic: buyers of illicit wine or yeast received sentences half as severe as producers.

sentences.zh: 三年，再下酒、曲之禁，凡私造差定其罪：城郭二十斤、鄉閭三十斤，棄市；

translations.literal: In year 3 they again issued prohibitions on wine and yeast; for all private manufacture crimes were graded: in cities twenty jin, in villages and hamlets thirty jin — execution in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: In 962 prohibitions on wine and yeast were reissued. Private manufacture: twenty jin in cities or thirty jin in the countryside meant execution;

sentences.zh: 民持私酒入京城五十里、西京及諸州城二十里者，至五斗處死；

translations.literal: If the people carried private wine within fifty li of the capital, or within twenty li of the Western Capital and prefectural cities, up to five dou meant death;
translations.idiomatic: carrying illicit wine within fifty li of the capital or twenty li of the Western Capital and prefectural seats: five dou or more meant death;

sentences.zh: 所定里數外，有官署酤酒而私酒入其地一石，棄市。

translations.literal: Outside the fixed number of li, where there was an official office selling wine, if private wine entered its territory one shi — execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: beyond those limits, one shi of illicit wine brought into an official sales zone meant execution.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，詔比建隆之禁第減之：凡至城郭五十斤以上、鄉閭百斤以上、私酒入禁地二石、三石以上、至有官署處四石，五石以上者，乃死。

translations.literal: In Qiande year 4 an edict compared to Jianlong prohibitions and reduced them step by step: only when reaching fifty jin or more in cities and towns, one hundred jin or more in villages and hamlets, private wine entering forbidden territory two shi or three shi or more, or at places with official offices four shi, five shi or more — then death.
translations.idiomatic: In 966 (Qiande 4) penalties were eased below Jianlong levels: death applied only at fifty jin or more in cities, one hundred jin in the countryside, two to three shi of illicit wine in restricted zones, or four to five shi near official sales offices.

sentences.zh: 法益輕而犯者鮮矣。

translations.literal: The law grew lighter and offenders were few.
translations.idiomatic: As the law grew milder, violations became rare.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年令：民買曲釀酒酤者，縣鎮十里如州城二十里之禁。

translations.literal: In Duangong year 2 an order said: for the people who bought yeast, brewed wine, and sold it, county market-towns within ten li were subject to the same prohibition as prefectural cities within twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: In 989 (Duangong 2) licensed brewers who bought yeast and sold wine faced the same ten-li restriction around county towns as the twenty-li rule around prefectural seats.

sentences.zh: 天聖以後，北京售曲如三京法，官售酒、曲亦畫疆界，戒相侵越，犯皆有法。

translations.literal: After Tiansheng, Beijing sold yeast like the three-capital law; official sale of wine and yeast also drew territorial boundaries, warning against mutual encroachment — violations all had law.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tiansheng era, Beijing followed the three-capital yeast rules; official wine and yeast sales were bounded by territories with penalties for encroachment.

sentences.zh: 其不禁之地，大概與宋初同，唯增永興軍、大通監、川峽之茂州、富順監。

translations.literal: The places without prohibition were largely the same as at the beginning of Song, only adding Yongxing Military Prefecture, Datong Directorate, Maozhou in the Sichuan gorges, and Fushun Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Exempt regions largely matched those of early Song, with Yongxing, Datong, Maozhou in Sichuan, and Fushun added.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平既久，戶口浸蕃，為酒醪以靡穀者益眾。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had been at peace long; population gradually grew; those who made wine and ale to consume grain grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace the population swelled, and ever more grain went into brewing.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，言者謂：「諸路酒課，月比歲增，無有藝極，非古者禁群飲、教節用之義。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing, memorialists said: "Wine levies on the various circuits increase month by month compared with the year — there is no limit of craft; this is not the ancient meaning of prohibiting group drinking and teaching frugal use."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianxing era critics noted that wine revenues on every circuit rose month on month without limit — contrary to the ancient ideal of curbing communal drinking and teaching thrift.

sentences.zh: 」遂詔：「鄉村毋得增置酒場，已募民主之者，期三年；

translations.literal: " An edict followed: "Villages must not add wine stations; those already recruited with the people as masters — set a term of three years;"
translations.idiomatic: " An edict followed: villages might not add new wine stations; existing licensed operators were given three-year terms;

sentences.zh: 他人雖欲增課以售，勿聽；

translations.literal: though others wished to increase the levy to sell, do not heed them;
translations.idiomatic: others might not raise levies to expand sales;

sentences.zh: 主者自欲增課，委官吏度異時不至虧額負課，然後上聞。

translations.literal: if masters themselves wished to increase the levy, commission officials to estimate that at another time they would not fall short of quota and owe the levy, then report upward.
translations.idiomatic: operators who wished to raise their own quotas had to show officials that future yields would cover the increase before petitioning the court.

sentences.zh: 」既而御史中丞晏殊請酒場利薄者悉禁增課。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward Censor-in-chief Yan Shu requested that wine stations with thin profit all be forbidden to increase levies.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor-in-chief Yan Shu then petitioned to forbid levy increases at low-margin wine stations.

sentences.zh: 天聖七年，詔：「民間有吉凶事酤酒，舊聽自便，毋抑配。

translations.literal: In Tiansheng year 7 an edict said: "When the people had auspicious or inauspicious affairs and bought wine, formerly they were heard to act as they pleased — do not compel apportioned sales."
translations.idiomatic: In 1029 (Tiansheng 7) an edict declared that households buying wine for weddings and funerals should not face forced quotas.

sentences.zh: 而江、淮、荊湖、兩浙酒戶往往豪製良民，至出引目，抑使多售。

translations.literal: Yet Jiang-Huai, Jing-Hu, and Two Zhe wine households often tyrannized good commoners, even issuing warrants and compelling them to buy more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Jiang-Huai, Jing-Hu, and the Two Zhe circuits wine franchisees often bullied commoners, issuing purchase orders and forcing excess sales.

sentences.zh: 其嚴禁止，犯者聽人告，募人代之。

translations.literal: Strictly prohibit this; offenders may be reported by the people, and recruits may replace them.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was strictly forbidden; violators could be reported, with informants recruited to take over franchises.

sentences.zh: 」慶曆初，三司言：「陝西用兵，軍費不給，尤資榷酤之利。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Qingli, the Three Departments said: "Shaanxi is at war; military expenses are insufficient — especially rely on monopoly-brewing profit."
translations.idiomatic: " Early in the Qingli era (1041–1048) the Three Departments reported that the Shaanxi campaign had strained military funds and that wine monopoly revenues were especially needed.

sentences.zh: 請較監臨官歲課，增者第賞之。

translations.literal: Request to compare supervising officials' annual levies; those who increased them were rewarded by grade.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to rank supervising officials by annual yields and reward those who increased revenues.

sentences.zh: 」繼令蕭定基、王琪等商度利害。

translations.literal: " They then ordered Xiao Dingji, Wang Qi, and others to deliberate benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Dingji, Wang Qi, and others were then ordered to assess the policy's costs and benefits.

sentences.zh: 初，酒場歲課不登，州縣多責衙前或伍保輸錢以充其數，嘉祐、治平中，數戒止之。

translations.literal: Initially, when wine-station annual levies were not fulfilled, prefectures and counties often charged yamen runners or ward-and-tithing groups to pay money to fill the quota; in Jiayou and Zhiping they repeatedly warned to stop this.
translations.idiomatic: When wine stations missed quotas, counties often forced yamen runners or ward-and-tithing groups to make up the shortfall; during the Jiayou and Zhiping eras repeated edicts forbade the practice.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，手詔蠲京師酒戶所負曲錢十六萬緡，又江南比歲所增酒場，強率人酤酒者禁止。

translations.literal: In Zhiping year 4, an imperial autograph edict remitted one hundred sixty thousand strings of yeast money owed by capital wine households; also in Jiangnan, for wine stations added in recent years, those who forcibly compelled people to buy wine were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067 (Zhiping 4) an imperial autograph remitted 160,000 strings of yeast debt owed by capital brewers and forbade the forced sales recently imposed at new Jiangnan wine stations.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，酒曲歲課合緡錢一千四百九十八萬六千一百九十六，至治平中，減二百一十二萬三千七百三；

translations.literal: In Huangyou, the annual wine-and-yeast levy totaled one million four hundred ninety-eight thousand six hundred sixteen strings of cash; by Zhiping it decreased by two million one hundred twenty-three thousand seven hundred three;
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangyou era annual wine and yeast revenues totaled 14,986,196 strings; by Zhiping they had fallen by 2,123,703;

sentences.zh: 而皇祐中，又入金帛、絲纊、芻粟、材木之類，總其數四百萬七百六十，治平中，乃增一百九十九萬一千九百七十五。

translations.literal: Yet in Huangyou they also received gold, silk, floss, fodder grain, timber and the like, totaling four million seven hundred sixty; in Zhiping it increased by one million nine hundred ninety-one thousand nine hundred seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyou also brought in gold, silk, fodder, timber, and similar goods worth 4,000,760; by Zhiping that in-kind revenue had risen by 1,991,975.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，詔諸郡遇節序毋得以酒相饋。

translations.literal: In Xining year 3 an edict said that on festivals the various prefectures must not use wine as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070 (Xining 3) an edict forbade prefectures from exchanging wine gifts on holidays.

sentences.zh: 初，知渭州蔡挺言：「陝西有醞公使酒交遺，至逾二十驛，道路煩苦。

translations.literal: Initially, Weizhou prefect Cai Ting said: "In Shaanxi there is brewing of public-service wine for mutual gifts, reaching more than twenty post stations — the roads are troubled and weary."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Weizhou prefect Cai Ting reported that Shaanxi officials exchanged brewed "public-service wine" along routes spanning more than twenty post stations, burdening transport.

sentences.zh: 」詔禁之。

translations.literal: " An edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: " The court forbade the practice.

sentences.zh: 至是，都官郎中沈行復言：「知莫州柴貽範饋他州酒至九百餘瓶，用兵夫逾一百人。

translations.literal: At this time Capital Office director Shen Xingfu again said: "Mozhou prefect Chai Yifan gifted other prefectures wine reaching more than nine hundred bottles, using laborers exceeding one hundred men."
translations.idiomatic: Now Capital Office director Shen Xingfu reported that Mozhou prefect Chai Yifan had sent more than 900 bottles of wine to other prefectures using over 100 corvée laborers.

sentences.zh: 」故並諸路禁焉。

translations.literal: " Therefore the prohibition was extended to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: " The ban was therefore extended empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 四年，三司承買酒曲坊場錢率千錢稅五十，儲以祿吏。

translations.literal: In year 4 the Three Departments, on wine-and-yeast franchise purchase money, taxed fifty per thousand cash and stored it to pay clerks' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1071 the Three Departments levied a tax of 50 cash per 1,000 on wine and yeast franchise purchases, reserving the proceeds for clerks' salaries.

sentences.zh: 六月，令式所刪定官周直孺言：「在京曲院酒戶鬻酒虧額，原於曲數多則酒亦多，多則價賤，賤則人戶損其利。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Statutes Office revising official Zhou Zhiru said: "Capital yeast-yard wine households sell wine at a deficit in quota; the origin is that when yeast amounts are great, wine is also great; when great, price is cheap; when cheap, households lose their profit."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Statutes Office reviser Zhou Zhiru explained that capital yeast-yard brewers missed revenue targets because excess yeast produced excess wine, depressing prices and eroding household profits.

sentences.zh: 為今之法，宜減數增價，使酒有限而必售，則人無耗折之患，而官額不虧。

translations.literal: For present law, it is fitting to reduce quantity and raise price, so that wine is limited yet must sell — then the people have no loss from spoilage, and the official quota is not deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The remedy was to cut volume and raise prices so supply stayed limited yet sold through — sparing households spoilage losses while preserving state quotas.

sentences.zh: 請以百八十萬斤為定額，閏年增十五萬斤。

translations.literal: He requested to take one million eight hundred thousand jin as the fixed quota; in intercalary years increase by one hundred fifty thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a fixed quota of 1.8 million jin, with an extra 150,000 jin in intercalary years.

sentences.zh: 舊直，斤百六十八，百以八十五為數，請增為二百，百用省數，以便入出。

translations.literal: The old straight price: per jin one hundred sixty-eight; per hundred use eighty-five as the count — he requested to raise it to two hundred; per hundred use abbreviated numbers for convenience in receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: The old price was 168 cash per jin, reckoned at 85 per hundred-weight; he asked to raise it to 200, using round hundred-weight units for easier accounting.

sentences.zh: 」七年，諸郡舊不釀酒者許釀，以公使錢率百緡為千石，溢額者以違制論。

translations.literal: " In year 7, prefectures that formerly did not brew wine were permitted to brew, using public-service funds at the rate of one hundred strings per thousand shi; those exceeding quota were judged under violation-of-regulations law.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1074 prefectures previously barred from brewing were allowed to do so at 100 strings of public-service funds per 1,000 shi, with excess treated as a regulatory violation.

sentences.zh: 在京酒戶歲用糯三十萬石。

translations.literal: Capital wine households annually used three hundred thousand shi of glutinous rice.
translations.idiomatic: Capital brewers consumed 300,000 shi of glutinous rice yearly.

sentences.zh: 九年，江、浙災傷，米直騰貴，詔選官至所產地預給錢，俟成稔折輸於官。

translations.literal: In year 9 Jiang-Zhe suffered disaster damage; rice prices soared; an edict selected officials to go to producing regions and advance money, waiting until the harvest was ripe to deliver in kind to the government.
translations.idiomatic: In 1076 Jiang-Zhe flood losses drove rice prices up; officials were sent to growing regions to advance cash, with grain to be delivered after harvest.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔勿行，止以所糴在京新米與已糴米半用之。

translations.literal: Before long an edict said not to implement it; only use newly purchased rice in the capital and already purchased rice, half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the scheme was canceled; capital brewers were to use equal parts newly purchased and existing grain stocks.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，增在京酒戶曲錢，較年額損曲三十萬斤，閏年益造萬斤。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng year 1 they increased capital wine households' yeast money; compared with the annual quota they reduced yeast by three hundred thousand jin; in intercalary years increase production by ten thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1078 capital brewers' yeast fees were raised while the annual yeast quota was cut by 300,000 jin, with an extra 10,000 jin in intercalary years.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔：「在京鬻曲，歲以百二十萬斤為額，斤直錢二百五十，俟鬻及舊額，令復舊價。

translations.literal: In year 2 an edict said: "In the capital selling yeast — annually take one million two hundred thousand jin as quota, per jin straight price two hundred fifty cash; when sales reach the old quota, order restoration of the old price."
translations.idiomatic: In 1079 an edict set the capital yeast quota at 1.2 million jin at 250 cash per jin, with prices to revert to the old rate once sales hit the former quota.

sentences.zh: 酒戶負糟、糯錢，更期以二年帶輸，並蠲未請曲數十萬斤。

translations.literal: Wine households owed spent-grain and glutinous-rice money; the term was changed to two years with installment payment, and they remitted one hundred thousand jin of yeast not yet requested.
translations.idiomatic: Brewers' debts for spent grain and glutinous rice were spread over two years in installments, and 100,000 jin of unclaimed yeast quota was remitted.

sentences.zh: 」先是，京師曲法，自熙寧四年更定後，多不能償，雖屢閣未請曲數，及損歲額為百五十萬斤，斤增錢至二百四十，未免逋負。

translations.literal: " Earlier, capital yeast law — since the Xining year 4 revision, many could not repay; though they repeatedly suspended unrequested yeast amounts and reduced the annual quota to one million five hundred thousand jin, and raised per-jin cash to two hundred forty, they still could not avoid arrears.
translations.idiomatic: " Since the 1071 capital yeast reform, many brewers could not meet payments despite repeated quota suspensions, a cut to 1.5 million jin, and a price of 240 cash per jin — arrears persisted.

sentences.zh: 至是，命畢仲衍與周直孺講求利病，請：「損額增直，均給七十店，令日輸錢，周歲而足，月輸不及數，計所負倍罰；

translations.literal: At this time Bi Zhongyan and Zhou Zhiru were ordered to investigate benefit and harm; they requested: "Reduce quota and raise straight price; distribute equally to seventy shops; order daily payment of money; within the year complete it; if monthly payment does not reach the amount, calculate what is owed and double the penalty;"
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongyan and Zhou Zhiru were ordered to review the system. They proposed cutting quotas, raising prices, dividing supply among seventy shops with daily payments due within the year, and double penalties for monthly shortfalls;

sentences.zh: 其炊醞非時、擅益器量及用私曲，皆立告賞法。

translations.literal: for brewing out of season, arbitrarily increasing vessel measures, and using private yeast — all established informant-reward law.
translations.idiomatic: informant rewards were established for off-season brewing, unauthorized vessel sizes, and private yeast.

sentences.zh: 」悉施行之，而裁其價。

translations.literal: " All was implemented, yet they trimmed the price.
translations.idiomatic: " The reforms took effect, with a modest price reduction.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔：「帶輸舊曲錢及倍罰錢，仍寬以半歲，未經免罰者蠲三之一。

translations.literal: In year 3 an edict said: "Installment payment of old yeast money and double-penalty money — still grant half a year of grace; for those not yet exempted from penalty, remit one-third."
translations.idiomatic: In 1080 installment payments on old yeast debts and double penalties were extended six months, with one-third of unpaid penalties remitted.

sentences.zh: 」五年，外居宗室酒，止許於舊宮院尊長及近屬寄醞。

translations.literal: " In year 5, wine of imperial clansmen living outside — they were only permitted to entrust brewing to elders of their former palace compounds and close kin.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1082 clansmen living outside the capital might brew wine only through elders of their former palace compounds or close kin.

sentences.zh: 增永興軍乾祐縣十酒場。

translations.literal: They added ten wine stations in Qianyou County, Yongxing Military Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ten wine stations were added in Qianyou County, Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 酒戶負糟、糯錢，更令三年之內增月限以輸，並除限內罰息，其倍罰曲錢已蠲三之一，下戶更免一分。

translations.literal: Wine households owed spent-grain and glutinous-rice money; they were again ordered within three years to increase monthly limits for payment, and penalty interest within the term was removed; double-penalty yeast money already had one-third remitted; lower households were further exempted one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: Brewers' spent-grain and glutinous-rice debts were spread over three years with extended monthly terms; in-term penalty interest was canceled; one-third of double yeast penalties was remitted and poorer households received an additional ten-percent reduction.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，刪監司鬻酒及三路饋遺條。

translations.literal: In Yuanyou year 1 they deleted provisions on circuit commissioners selling wine and the three circuits' gift-giving.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086 provisions on circuit commissioners selling wine and gift exchanges along the three frontier circuits were removed.

sentences.zh: 紹聖二年，左司諫翟思言：諸郡釀酒，非沿邊並復熙寧之數。

translations.literal: In Shaosheng year 2, Left Office remonstrator Zhai Si said: prefectural brewing — except along the border, all restore Xining quotas.
translations.idiomatic: In 1095 Left Office remonstrator Zhai Si urged restoring Xining brewing quotas in all non-border prefectures.

sentences.zh: 詔：「熙寧五年以前，諸郡不釀酒、及有公使錢而無酒者，所釀並依《熙寧編敕》數。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Before Xining year 5, prefectures that did not brew wine and those with public-service funds but no wine — all brewing follows the Xining Compiled Statutes numbers."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered prefectures that had not brewed before 1072, or had public-service funds but no wine supply, to follow Xining statute quotas.

sentences.zh: 仍令諸郡所減勿逾百石，舊不及數者如舊，毋得於例外供饋。

translations.literal: Still order that reductions by prefectures must not exceed one hundred shi; those formerly below quota remain as before; they must not supply gifts beyond exceptions.
translations.idiomatic: Reductions were capped at 100 shi; prefectures already below quota were unchanged; extraordinary gift supplies were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」後又以陝西沿邊官監酒務課入不足，乃令邊郡非帥府並酌條製定釀酒數，諸將並城砦止許於官務寄釀。

translations.literal: " Later, because Shaanxi border official-supervised wine offices' revenue was insufficient, they ordered border prefectures that were not commanderies to fix brewing amounts according to regulations, and all generals and walled stockades were only permitted to entrust brewing at official offices.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, because border wine-office revenues in Shaanxi fell short, non-commandery border prefectures set brewing quotas by regulation, and frontier generals and stockades could brew only through official offices.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，知漣水軍錢景允言建立學舍，請以承買醋坊錢給用。

translations.literal: In Chongning year 2, Lianshui Military Prefecture prefect Qian Jingyun said he was establishing a school building and requested to use franchise-purchase vinegar-workshop money for expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1103 Lianshui prefect Qian Jingyun, building a school, asked to fund it from vinegar-franchise receipts.

sentences.zh: 詔常平司計無害公費如所請，仍令他路準行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ever-Normal Granary office to calculate that public expenses would not be harmed as requested, and still order other circuits to follow as model.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal office was to confirm no harm to public funds, with other circuits allowed to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 初，元祐臣僚請罷榷醋，戶部謂本無禁文。

translations.literal: Initially, Yuanyou court officials requested to abolish the vinegar monopoly; the Revenue Ministry said there originally was no prohibition text.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuanyou officials had sought to end the vinegar monopoly, but the Revenue Ministry noted that no prohibition statute existed.

sentences.zh: 後翟思請以諸郡醋坊日息用餘悉歸常平，至是，景允有請，故令常平計之。

translations.literal: Later Zhai Si requested that daily surplus from vinegar workshops in the various prefectures all go to Ever-Normal; at this time Jingyun had a request, so they ordered Ever-Normal to calculate it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhai Si had proposed routing vinegar-workshop daily surpluses to the Ever-Normal fund; Jingyun's petition now required the Ever-Normal office to assess it.

sentences.zh: 十月，諸路官監酒直，上者升增錢二，中下增一，以充學費，餘裨轉運司歲用。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on wine straight prices under official supervision on the various circuits — upper grade raised by two cash, middle and lower by one — to fill school expenses; the remainder supplemented transport commissioners' annual use.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month official wine prices on all circuits were raised two cash in upper-tier markets and one in middle and lower tiers to fund schools, with the remainder for transport commissioners.

sentences.zh: 大觀四年，以兩浙轉運司之請，官監鬻糟錢別立額比較。

translations.literal: In Daguan year 4, on the Two Zhe transport commissioner's request, official-supervised spent-grain sales money had a separate quota established for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1110, at the Two Zhe transport commissioner's request, a separate quota was set for official spent-grain sales revenue.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「諸郡榷酒之池，入出酒米，並別遣倉官。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Monopoly-wine pools in the various prefectures — incoming and outgoing wine grain — all separately dispatch granary officials."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict required separate granary officers to oversee grain entering and leaving monopoly brewing pools in every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賣醋毋得越郡城五里外，凡縣、鎮、村並禁，其息悉歸轉運司，舊屬常平者如故。

translations.literal: Selling vinegar must not go beyond five li outside the prefectural city; all counties, market towns, and villages were likewise forbidden, and all profit was to go entirely to the transport commission; what had formerly belonged to the Ever-Normal Granaries remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Vinegar could not be sold more than five li beyond a prefectural seat; the ban applied to counties, market towns, and villages alike. All proceeds went to the transport commission, while revenues previously assigned to the Ever-Normal Granaries were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，淮南發運副使董正封言：「杭州都酒務甲於諸路，治平前歲課三十萬緡，今不過二十萬。

translations.literal: In Zhenghe year 2, Huainan dispatch deputy commissioner Dong Zhengfeng said: "Hangzhou's metropolitan wine bureau ranks first among all circuits; before the Zhiping era its annual quota was three hundred thousand strings, but now it does not reach two hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: In 1112, Huainan dispatch deputy commissioner Dong Zhengfeng reported: "Hangzhou's metropolitan wine bureau led every circuit in revenue. Before the Zhiping era it yielded three hundred thousand strings a year; now it brings in barely two hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 請令分務為三，更置比較務二，毋增官吏兵匠，仍請本路諸郡並增務比較。

translations.literal: He requested that the bureau be divided into three offices, that two comparison bureaus be newly established without adding officials, clerks, soldiers, or artisans, and that all prefectures in the circuit likewise add comparison offices.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the bureau be split into three offices and two new comparison bureaus be set up without increasing staff, soldiers, or artisans, and that every prefecture in the circuit establish comparable offices for revenue auditing.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，兩浙轉運司亦請置務比較，定課額釀酒收息，以增虧為賞罰。

translations.literal: In year 4, the Two Zhe transport commission also requested establishing comparison bureaus, fixing quota revenues from brewing and collecting profit, and using surplus or deficit as the basis for rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1114 the Two Zhe transport commission likewise petitioned for comparison bureaus, fixed brewing quotas and profit targets, and tied rewards and penalties to gains or shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 詔：「酒務官二員者分兩務，三員者復增其一，員雖多毋得過四務。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Where a wine bureau had two officials, divide it into two offices; where it had three, add one more; however many officials there were, there must be no more than four offices."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Bureaus with two officials were to be split into two offices; those with three were to add a fourth office. No bureau, however many officials it had, could exceed four offices."

sentences.zh: 內有官雖多而課息不廣者，聽如舊。

translations.literal: Among these, where there were many officials but quota revenue was not broad, they were permitted to remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus with many officials but modest revenues were allowed to keep their existing arrangements.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，以湖南路諸務糟酵錢分入提舉司，令斤增錢三，為直達糧綱水工之費。

translations.literal: " That year, the mash-and-yeast money of the various bureaus in Hunan Circuit was divided and entered the intendant's office; each jin was ordered to add three cash to cover the expenses of direct-transport grain convoys and boatmen.
translations.idiomatic: That year, mash-and-yeast revenues from Hunan wine bureaus were reassigned to the intendant's office, with a three-cash surcharge per jin to pay direct-transport grain convoys and boat crews.

sentences.zh: 立酒匠闕聽選試清務廂軍之法。

translations.literal: Regulations were established for filling vacancies among brewers by allowing selection and examination from the Clear-Service corvee militia.
translations.idiomatic: Rules were set for recruiting brewers from the Clear-Service corvee militia whenever posts fell vacant.

sentences.zh: 清務者，本州選刺供踏曲爨蒸之役，闕則募人以充。

translations.literal: Clear Service meant that the prefecture selected and branded men to supply labor for kneading yeast and firing boilers for steaming; when there were vacancies, people were recruited to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Clear Service referred to men selected and registered by the prefecture for yeast-kneading and brewing work; vacancies were filled by recruitment.

sentences.zh: 渡江後，屈於養兵，隨時增課，名目雜出，或主於提刑，或領於漕司，或分隸於經、總製司，惟恐軍資有所未裕。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, constrained by the need to maintain armies, levies were increased from time to time and names proliferated in disorder; some were overseen by the intendant of punishments, some led by the transport commission, and some divided among the fiscal management offices — all for fear that military funds might fall short.
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled south across the Yangzi, army upkeep forced repeated levy increases under a tangle of new names. Some revenues were managed by circuit intendant offices, some by transport commissions, and some by fiscal management bureaus — all to keep military funds from running dry.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，總領四川財賦趙開遂大變酒法：自成都始，先罷公帑實供給酒，即舊撲買坊場所置隔釀，設官主之，民以米入官自釀，斛輸錢三十，頭子錢二十二。

translations.literal: In Jianyan year 3, overall director of Sichuan finances Zhao Kai then greatly changed the wine law: starting from Chengdu, he first abolished wine supplied in kind from the public treasury; at the old leased franchise sites he set up separate brewing, placed officials in charge, and had the people bring rice to the government to brew themselves, paying thirty cash per hu and a surcharge of twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In 1129, Zhao Kai, overall director of Sichuan finances, overhauled the wine monopoly. Starting in Chengdu, he ended direct government supply of wine, converted former leased franchises into separate-brewing sites under official supervision, and required households to deliver rice and brew under state license — thirty cash per hu plus a twenty-two-cash surcharge.

sentences.zh: 明年，遍下其法於四路，歲遞增至六百九十餘萬緡，凡官槽四百所，私店不預焉，於是東南之酒額亦日增矣。

translations.literal: The next year the law was extended throughout the four circuits, increasing year by year to more than six million nine hundred thousand strings; there were four hundred government brewing vats in all, and private shops did not participate; thus the wine quotas of the southeast also grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the system spread across all four Sichuan circuits, with annual revenue rising to more than 6.9 million strings. Four hundred government brewing vats were established; private shops were excluded. Southeast wine quotas climbed steadily thereafter.

sentences.zh: 四年，以米曲價高，詔上等升增二十文，上等升增十八文，俟米曲價平依舊。

translations.literal: In year 4, because rice and yeast prices were high, an edict ordered upper grade to rise twenty cash and upper grade to rise eighteen cash — to return to the old rule when rice and yeast prices were level.
translations.idiomatic: In 1130, with rice and yeast prices high, the court raised upper-grade wine twenty cash per sheng and lower-grade wine eighteen, to revert once grain and yeast prices normalized.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，兩浙酒坊於買撲上添淨利錢五分，季輸送戶部。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing year 1, the Two Zhe wine franchises added five tenths of net profit on top of the lease price, remitted quarterly to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131, Two Zhe wine franchises were assessed an additional five percent of net profit on their lease payments, sent quarterly to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又增諸酒錢上升二十文，下十文。

translations.literal: Wine prices were further raised twenty cash per sheng for upper grades and ten for lower grades.
translations.idiomatic: Wine prices were raised again — twenty cash per sheng for upper grades and ten for lower grades.

sentences.zh: 其諸州軍賣酒虧折，隨宜增價，一分州用，一分漕計，一分隸經制司。

translations.literal: Where wine sales in the various prefectures and armies showed losses, prices were raised as appropriate; one part went to prefectural use, one part to transport accounts, and one part to the fiscal management office.
translations.idiomatic: Where prefectures and garrisons lost money on wine sales, prices were raised as needed; one third went to prefectural funds, one third to transport accounts, and one third to fiscal management offices.

sentences.zh: 先是，酒有定價，每增須上請。

translations.literal: Previously, wine had fixed prices, and every increase had to be reported upward for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Previously wine prices had been fixed, and any increase required central approval.

sentences.zh: 是後，郡縣始自增，而價不一矣。

translations.literal: After this, prefectures and counties began to raise prices on their own, and prices were no longer uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter prefectures and counties began raising prices on their own, and wine prices ceased to be uniform.

sentences.zh: 五年，令諸州酒不以上下，升增五文，隸製總司。

translations.literal: In year 5, all prefectural wine, regardless of grade, was ordered raised five cash per sheng, assigned to the fiscal management office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1135, every prefecture was ordered to add five cash per sheng to all grades of wine, with the revenue assigned to fiscal management offices.

sentences.zh: 六年，以紹興二年以後三年中一年中數立額，其增羨給郡縣用。

translations.literal: In year 6, taking the median year among the three years after Shaoxing year 2 as the quota, surplus above it was given for prefectural and county use.
translations.idiomatic: In 1136, quotas were set from the median annual yield of the three years after 1132; any surplus was reserved for prefectural and county expenses.

sentences.zh: 罷四川州、軍、縣、鎮酒官百七員，其酒息微處並罷之。

translations.literal: One hundred seven wine officials in Sichuan prefectures, armies, counties, and market towns were abolished, and places where wine revenue was slight were abolished as well.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred seven Sichuan wine posts at prefectures, garrisons, counties, and market towns were eliminated, along with every office whose wine revenue was negligible.

sentences.zh: 七年，以戶部尚書章誼等言，行在置贍軍酒庫。

translations.literal: In year 7, on the memorial of Minister of Revenue Zhang Yi and others, an Army-Support wine warehouse was established at the temporary capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1137, following a proposal by Minister of Revenue Zhang Yi and others, an Army-Support wine warehouse was established at the court in exile.

sentences.zh: 四川製置使胡世將即成都、潼川、資、普、廣安立清酒務，許民買撲，歲為錢四萬八千餘緡。

translations.literal: Sichuan commissioner Hu Shijiang immediately established Clear-Wine bureaus at Chengdu, Tongchuan, Zi, Pu, and Guang'an, allowing the people to lease them by bid, yielding more than forty-eight thousand strings a year.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan commissioner Hu Shijiang set up Clear-Wine bureaus at Chengdu, Tongchuan, Zi, Pu, and Guang'an, leasing them to private operators for more than forty-eight thousand strings annually.

sentences.zh: 自趙開行隔槽法，增至十四萬六千餘緡，

translations.literal: From the time Zhao Kai implemented the separate-vat law, revenue increased to more than one hundred forty-six thousand strings,
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Kai introduced the separate-vat system, revenue rose to more than 146,000 strings,

sentences.zh: （紹興元年。）〉

translations.literal: (Shaoxing year 1.)
translations.idiomatic: (Shaoxing 1.)

sentences.zh: 及世將改官監，所入又倍，自後累增至五十四萬八千餘緡，

translations.literal: When Shijiang changed to official supervision, receipts doubled again; afterward they accumulated to more than five hundred forty-eight thousand strings,
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Shijiang switched to direct official supervision, receipts doubled again and eventually reached more than 548,000 strings,

sentences.zh: （紹興二十五年。）〉

translations.literal: (Shaoxing year 25.)
translations.idiomatic: (Shaoxing 25.)

sentences.zh: 而外邑及民戶坊場又為三十九萬緡。

translations.literal: while outlying towns and civilian franchise sites yielded another three hundred ninety thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: While outlying towns and privately leased franchises brought in another 390,000 strings.

sentences.zh: （淳熙二年。）〉

translations.literal: (Chunxi year 2.)
translations.idiomatic: (Chunxi 2.)

sentences.zh: 然隔槽之法始行，聽就務分槽醞賣，官計所入之米而收其課，若未病也。

translations.literal: Yet when the separate-vat law was first implemented, people were allowed to brew and sell at divided vats within the bureau; the government counted the rice brought in and collected the levy — the people were not yet harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the separate-vat system was first introduced, households brewed and sold at divided vats within official bureaus; the state measured incoming rice and collected the levy — a burden the public had not yet felt.

sentences.zh: 行之既久，醞賣虧欠，則責入米之家認輸，不復核其米而第取其錢，民始病矣。

translations.literal: After it had been in force for long, when brewing and sales showed deficits, households that had delivered rice were held liable to make up the shortfall; the government no longer verified the rice but simply took the cash — then the people began to suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Over time, when brewing revenues fell short, households that had delivered rice were forced to cover the deficit. Officials stopped verifying grain deliveries and simply collected cash — and the public began to feel the strain.

sentences.zh: 十年，罷措置贍軍酒庫所，官吏悉歸戶部，以左曹郎中兼領，以點檢贍軍酒庫為名，與本路漕臣共其事。

translations.literal: In year 10, the Army-Support wine warehouse planning office was abolished; all officials and clerks returned to the Ministry of Revenue, with a left-section bureau director concurrently in charge under the name Inspector of Army-Support Wine Warehouses, sharing the work with the circuit transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1140, the Army-Support wine planning office was abolished and its staff transferred to the Ministry of Revenue. A left-section bureau director took concurrent charge under the title Inspector of Army-Support Wine Warehouses, working jointly with the circuit transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十五年，弛夔路酒禁。

translations.literal: In year 15, the wine prohibition in the Kuizhou circuit was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1145, the wine monopoly in the Kuizhou circuit was lifted.

sentences.zh: 以南北十一庫並充贍軍激賞酒庫，隸左右司。

translations.literal: Eleven warehouses north and south were combined as Army-Support and Merit-Reward wine warehouses, subordinate to the Left and Right Secretariat offices.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven warehouses north and south of the capital were combined into Army-Support and Merit-Reward wine stores, placed under the Left and Right Secretariat offices.

sentences.zh: 十七年，省四川清酒務監官，成都府二員，興元遂寧府、漢、綿、邛、蜀、彭、簡、果州、富順監並漢州綿州、縣各一員。

translations.literal: In year 17, Sichuan Clear-Wine bureau supervisory posts were reduced: two at Chengdu Prefecture; one each at Xingyuan, Suining Prefecture, Han, Mian, Qiong, Shu, Peng, Jian, Guo Prefecture, Fushun Supervisorate, and the counties of Han and Mian Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In 1147, Sichuan Clear-Wine supervisory posts were cut back to two at Chengdu and one each at Xingyuan, Suining, Han, Mian, Qiong, Shu, Peng, Jian, Guo, the Fushun supervisorate, and the counties of Han and Mian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔諸軍買撲酒坊監官賞格依舊。

translations.literal: In year 21, an edict restored the old reward scales for supervisory officials of army-leased wine franchises.
translations.idiomatic: In 1151, an edict restored the previous reward scales for supervisors of army-leased wine franchises.

sentences.zh: （四萬、三萬貫已上場務：增及一倍，減一年磨勘，二倍減二年磨勘，三倍減三年磨勘，四倍減四年磨勘。

translations.literal: (For franchise sites of forty thousand and thirty thousand strings and above: if revenue doubled, merit review was shortened by one year; if it tripled, by two years; if it quadrupled, by three years; if it quintupled, by four years.
translations.idiomatic: (For franchises yielding forty thousand or thirty thousand strings and above: doubling revenue shortened merit review by one year; tripling by two years; quadrupling by three years; quintupling by four years.

sentences.zh: 二萬、一萬貫已上場務：增及一倍，減三季磨勘，二倍減一年磨勘，三倍減三年磨勘，七千貫以上場務：增及一倍，升三季名次，二倍減一年磨勘，三倍減一年半磨勘，四倍減二年磨勘。

translations.literal: For sites of twenty thousand and ten thousand strings and above: if revenue doubled, merit review was shortened by three seasons; if it tripled, by one year; if it quadrupled, by three years. For sites of seven thousand strings and above: if revenue doubled, rank was raised by three seasons; if it tripled, merit review was shortened by one year; if it quadrupled, by one and a half years; if it quintupled, by two years.
translations.idiomatic: For franchises of twenty thousand or ten thousand strings and above: doubling revenue cut merit review by three seasons; tripling by one year; quadrupling by three years. For franchises of seven thousand strings and above: doubling raised rank by three seasons; tripling shortened review by one year; quadrupling by eighteen months; quintupling by two years.

sentences.zh: 七千貫以下場務：增及一萬貫減一年磨勘，二萬貫減二年磨勘，三萬貫減三年磨勘，四萬貫減四年磨勘。）〉

translations.literal: For sites below seven thousand strings: an increase of ten thousand strings shortened merit review by one year; twenty thousand by two years; thirty thousand by three years; forty thousand by four years.)
translations.idiomatic: For franchises below seven thousand strings: increases of ten thousand strings shortened review by one year; twenty thousand by two years; thirty thousand by three years; forty thousand by four years.)

sentences.zh: 二十五年，罷諸路漕司寄造酒。

translations.literal: In year 25, commissioned brewing by circuit transport commissions was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1155, commissioned brewing by circuit transport commissions was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以隔槽酒擾民，許買撲以便民。

translations.literal: In year 27, because separate-vat wine troubled the people, leasing by bid was permitted to ease the burden.
translations.idiomatic: In 1157, with the separate-vat system burdening the public, franchises were opened to competitive lease to ease the hardship.

sentences.zh: 罷官監，後復製之。

translations.literal: Official supervision was abolished, then later restored.
translations.idiomatic: Direct official supervision was abolished, then later reinstated.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以點檢措置贍軍酒庫改隸戶部。

translations.literal: In year 30, the Inspector and Planner of Army-Support Wine Warehouses was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1160, the Inspector and Planner of Army-Support Wine Warehouses was placed under the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 既而戶部侍郎邵大受等言：「歲計賴經、總製，窠名至多，今諸路歲虧二百萬，皆緣諸州公使庫廣造，別置店酤賣，以致酒務例皆敗壞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Vice Minister of Revenue Shao Dashou and others said: "Annual budgets rely on fiscal management offices, and revenue categories are extremely numerous. Now the various circuits lose two million a year, all because prefectures' public-service warehouses brew on a large scale and set up separate shops to retail wine, causing wine bureaus everywhere to fail.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Vice Minister Shao Dashou and others reported: "Annual budgets depend on fiscal management offices, and revenue categories have multiplied. Circuits now lose two million strings a year because prefectures' public-service warehouses brew heavily and open separate retail shops, driving official wine bureaus to ruin.

sentences.zh: 」詔罷諸州別置酒庫，如軍糧酒庫、防月庫、月樁庫之類，並省務寄造酒及帥司激買酒庫。

translations.literal: " An edict abolished separately established wine warehouses in the prefectures, such as army-grain wine warehouses, frontier-defense monthly warehouses, and monthly-stockpile warehouses, and also abolished commissioned brewing at provincial bureaus and the commander's merit-purchase wine warehouses.
translations.idiomatic: " The court abolished separately established prefectural wine stores — army-grain wine warehouses, frontier-defense monthly stores, monthly stockpile stores, and the like — along with commissioned brewing at provincial bureaus and commanders' merit-purchase wine warehouses.

sentences.zh: 凡未分隸經、總制錢處，並立額分隸，補趁虧額。

translations.literal: Wherever revenues had not yet been divided among fiscal management offices, quotas were established and revenues divided to make up deficits.
translations.idiomatic: Where revenues had not yet been assigned to fiscal management offices, fixed quotas were set and revenues reassigned to cover shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，殿帥趙密以諸軍酒坊六十六歸之戶部，

translations.literal: In year 31, Palace Guard commander Zhao Mi turned sixty-six army wine franchises over to the Ministry of Revenue,
translations.idiomatic: In 1161, Palace Guard commander Zhao Mi transferred sixty-six army wine franchises to the Ministry of Revenue,

sentences.zh: （見九年。）〉

translations.literal: (See year 9.)
translations.idiomatic: (See year 9.)

sentences.zh: 同安郡王楊存中罷殿帥，復以私撲酒坊九上之；

translations.literal: Prince of Tong'an Yang Cunzhong, upon leaving the post of Palace Guard commander, again turned over nine privately leased wine franchises;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Tong'an Yang Cunzhong stepped down as Palace Guard commander, he likewise surrendered nine privately leased wine franchises;

sentences.zh: 歲通收息六十萬緡有奇，以十分為率，七分輸送行在，三分給漕計。

translations.literal: annual total profit exceeded six hundred thousand strings; taking ten parts as the rate, seven parts were sent to the temporary capital and three parts to transport accounts.
translations.idiomatic: their combined annual profit exceeded six hundred thousand strings. Seven tenths went to the court in exile and three tenths to transport accounts.

sentences.zh: 蓋自軍興以來，諸帥擅榷酤之利，由是，縣官始得資之以佐經費焉。

translations.literal: From the time military campaigns began, commanders had monopolized wine profits for themselves; only then did the state treasury begin to draw on these revenues to supplement regular expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, field commanders had kept wine monopolies for themselves. Only then did the central treasury begin tapping those revenues to help meet routine expenses.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乾道元年，以浙東、西犒賞庫六十四隸三衙，輸課於左藏南庫，餘錢充隨年贍軍及造軍器。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao under Emperor Xiaozong, sixty-four reward warehouses in eastern and western Zhe were placed under the Three Guards; levies were sent to the Left Treasury South Storehouse, and remaining funds supplied annual army support and arms manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1165, sixty-four reward wine warehouses in eastern and western Zhe were assigned to the Three Guards. Their levies went to the Left Treasury South Storehouse; surplus funds paid annual army support and arms production.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔：「臨安府安撫司酒庫悉歸贍軍；

translations.literal: In year 2, an edict said: "All wine warehouses of the Lin'an Prefecture pacification commission shall revert to Army Support;
translations.idiomatic: In 1166, an edict ordered: "All wine warehouses of the Lin'an pacification commission were to be transferred to Army Support;

sentences.zh: 並贍軍諸庫及臨安府安撫司酒務，令戶部取三年所收一年中數立額。

translations.literal: together with all Army-Support warehouses and the Lin'an pacification commission wine bureaus, the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to set quotas from the median year among three years of receipts.
translations.idiomatic: along with all Army-Support warehouses and Lin'an pacification commission wine bureaus, the Ministry of Revenue was to set quotas from the median annual yield of the previous three years.

sentences.zh: 」日售錢萬緡，歲收本錢一百四十萬，息錢一百六十萬，曲錢二萬，羨餘獻以內藏者又二十萬，其後增為五十萬。

translations.literal: " Daily sales reached ten thousand strings; annual principal receipts were one million four hundred thousand, profit one million six hundred thousand, yeast money twenty thousand, and surplus presented to the Inner Treasury another two hundred thousand — later increased to five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " Daily sales reached ten thousand strings. Annual principal totaled 1.4 million strings, profit 1.6 million, yeast fees twenty thousand, and surplus presented to the Inner Treasury another two hundred thousand — later raised to five hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 四年，立場務官賞格。

translations.literal: In year 4, reward scales for franchise officials were established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1168, reward scales for franchise supervisors were established.

sentences.zh: 七年，以淮西總領周言，總所庫四，安撫司庫五，都統司庫十八，馬軍司庫一，增置行宮庫一，共為庫二十九，以三年最高年為額；

translations.literal: In year 7, on the proposal of Huai West overall director Zhou Yan, there were four overall-director warehouses, five pacification-commission warehouses, eighteen supreme-command warehouses, one cavalry-command warehouse, and one newly added traveling-palace warehouse — twenty-nine warehouses in all — with quotas set from the highest year among three;
translations.idiomatic: In 1171, following a proposal by Huai West overall director Zhou Yan, four overall-director warehouses, five pacification-commission warehouses, eighteen supreme-command warehouses, one cavalry-command warehouse, and one new traveling-palace warehouse — twenty-nine in all — were placed on quotas based on the highest of three years' receipts;

sentences.zh: 其行宮新庫息錢，除分認諸處錢及縻費，以淨息三分為率，一分輸御前酒庫；

translations.literal: of the profit from the new traveling-palace warehouse, after allotments to various places and overhead expenses, net profit was divided in three parts, one part sent to the Imperial Front wine warehouse;
translations.idiomatic: net profit from the new traveling-palace warehouse, after assigned payments and overhead, was divided in thirds, with one third sent to the Imperial Front wine warehouse;

sentences.zh: 以提領建康府戶部贍軍酒庫為名，遂鑄印及改庫名。

translations.literal: under the name Director of Jiankang Prefecture Ministry-of-Revenue Army-Support Wine Warehouse, seals were cast and the warehouse name changed.
translations.idiomatic: the office was titled Director of the Jiankang Ministry-of-Revenue Army-Support Wine Warehouse; new seals were cast and the warehouse renamed.

sentences.zh: 八年，知常德府劉邦翰言：「湖北之民困於酒坊，至貧乏家，不捐萬錢則不能舉一吉凶之禮。

translations.literal: In year 8, Changde prefect Liu Banghan said: "The people of Hubei are distressed by wine franchises; even poor households cannot perform a single ceremony of joy or mourning unless they pay ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In 1172, Changde prefect Liu Banghan reported: "The people of Hubei are crushed by wine franchises. Even the poorest families must pay ten thousand cash before they can hold a wedding or funeral.

sentences.zh: 」乃檢《乾道重修敕令》，申嚴抑買之禁。

translations.literal: " He then examined the Qiandao Revised Statutes and Decrees and strictly enforced the prohibition on forced purchase.
translations.idiomatic: " He cited the Qiandao Revised Statutes and Decrees and strictly enforced the ban on coerced purchases.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年詔：「四川酒課折估困弊，可減額錢四十七萬三千五百餘緡，令禮部給降度牒六百六十一道，補還今歲減數，明年於四川合給湖廣總所錢補之。」

translations.literal: In Chunxi year 3 an edict said: "Sichuan wine levies, devalued in assessment, are in distress; quota revenue may be reduced by four hundred seventy-three thousand five hundred plus strings. Let the Ministry of Rites issue six hundred sixty-one ordination certificates to make up this year's reduction; next year it shall be made up from funds Sichuan owes the Huguang overall office."
translations.idiomatic: In 1176 an edict declared: "Sichuan wine revenues, depressed by devalued assessments, may be cut by more than 473,500 strings. The Ministry of Rites was to issue 661 ordination certificates to cover this year's shortfall; next year the sum would be recovered from Sichuan's payments to the Huguang overall office."

sentences.zh: 寧宗開禧元年，知臨安府兼點檢贍軍激賞庫趙善防、轉運判官提領戶部犒賞酒庫詹徽之言，官吏冗費，請諸司官屬兼管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi under Emperor Ningzong, Lin'an prefect and concurrent Inspector of Army-Support and Merit-Reward Warehouses Zhao Shanfang and transport vice-commissioner and Director of Ministry-of-Revenue Reward Wine Warehouses Zhan Hui petitioned that redundant officials and expenses be cut by having staff of various offices serve concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In 1205, Lin'an prefect and concurrent Inspector of Army-Support and Merit-Reward Warehouses Zhao Shanfang and transport vice-commissioner Zhan Hui, who also directed Ministry-of-Revenue reward wine warehouses, petitioned to cut redundant staff by assigning concurrent duties to officials of various offices.

sentences.zh: 明年，又以都省言課額失陷，依舊辟置。

translations.literal: The next year, because the Secretariat reported that quotas had fallen short, separate appointments were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with the Secretariat reporting shortfalls against quota, dedicated posts were restored.

sentences.zh: 初，趙開之立隔釀法也，蓋以紓一時之急，其後行之諸郡，國家贍兵，郡縣經費，率取給於此。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhao Kai established the separate-brewing law, it was meant to relieve a momentary crisis; afterward it was applied in the various prefectures, and state support for armies and prefectural and county expenses generally drew upon it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Kai first established separate brewing, it was meant to ease a temporary crisis. The system soon spread through the prefectures, and both army support and local budgets came to depend on it.

sentences.zh: 故雖罷行、增減，不一而足，而其法卒不可廢雲。

translations.literal: Thus although it was abolished, implemented, increased, and reduced in more ways than can be counted, the law in the end could not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Though the system was suspended, revived, expanded, and cut back in countless ways, it could never finally be abolished.

sentences.zh: 坑冶凡金、銀、銅、鐵、鉛、錫監冶場務二百有一：金產商、饒、歙、撫四州，南安軍。

translations.literal: For mines and smelting, there were in all two hundred one supervisory smelting offices and sites for gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin: gold was produced in the four prefectures Shang, Rao, She, and Fu, and Nan'an Military District.
translations.idiomatic: Mines and smelting comprised 201 supervisory offices and sites for gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin. Gold came from Shang, Rao, She, and Fu prefectures and Nan'an Military District.

sentences.zh: 銀產鳳、建、桂陽三州，有三監；

translations.literal: Silver was produced in the three prefectures Feng, Jian, and Guiyang, with three supervisory offices;
translations.idiomatic: Silver came from Feng, Jian, and Guiyang prefectures, with three supervisory offices;

sentences.zh: 饒、信、虔、越、衢、處、道、福、汀、漳、南劍、韶、廣、英、連、恩、春十七州，建昌、邵武、南安三軍，有五十一場；

translations.literal: seventeen prefectures — Rao, Xin, Qian, Yue, Qu, Chu, Dao, Fu, Ting, Zhang, Nanjian, Shao, Guang, Ying, Lian, En, and Chun — and three military districts — Jianchang, Shaowu, and Nan'an — had fifty-one sites;
translations.idiomatic: fifty-one sites in seventeen prefectures — Rao, Xin, Qian, Yue, Qu, Chu, Dao, Fu, Ting, Zhang, Nanjian, Shao, Guang, Ying, Lian, En, and Chun — and three military districts — Jianchang, Shaowu, and Nan'an;

sentences.zh: 秦、隴、興元三州，有三務。

translations.literal: the three prefectures Qin, Long, and Xingyuan had three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: and three bureaus in Qin, Long, and Xingyuan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 銅產饒、處、建、英、信、汀、漳、南劍八州，南安、邵武二軍，有三十五場；

translations.literal: Copper was produced in eight prefectures — Rao, Chu, Jian, Ying, Xin, Ting, Zhang, and Nanjian — and two military districts — Nan'an and Shaowu — with thirty-five sites;
translations.idiomatic: Copper came from thirty-five sites in Rao, Chu, Jian, Ying, Xin, Ting, Zhang, and Nanjian prefectures and Nan'an and Shaowu military districts;

sentences.zh: 梓州有一務。

translations.literal: Zizhou had one bureau.
translations.idiomatic: and one bureau in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 鐵產徐、兗、相三州，有四監；

translations.literal: Iron was produced in the three prefectures Xu, Yan, and Xiang, with four supervisory offices;
translations.idiomatic: Iron came from four supervisory offices in Xu, Yan, and Xiang prefectures;

sentences.zh: 河南、鳳翔、同、虢、儀、蘄、黃、袁、英九州，興國軍，有十二冶；

translations.literal: nine prefectures — Henan, Fengxiang, Tong, Guo, Yi, Qi, Huang, Yuan, and Ying — and Xingguo Military District had twelve smelteries;
translations.idiomatic: twelve smelteries in Henan, Fengxiang, Tong, Guo, Yi, Qi, Huang, Yuan, and Ying prefectures and Xingguo Military District;

sentences.zh: 晉、磁、鳳、澧、道、渠、合、梅、陝、耀、坊、虔、汀、吉十四州，有二十務；

translations.literal: fourteen prefectures — Jin, Ci, Feng, Li, Dao, Qu, He, Mei, Shan, Yao, Fang, Qian, Ting, and Ji — had twenty bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: twenty bureaus in Jin, Ci, Feng, Li, Dao, Qu, He, Mei, Shan, Yao, Fang, Qian, Ting, and Ji prefectures;

sentences.zh: 信、鄂、連、建、南劍五州，邵武軍，有二十五場。

translations.literal: five prefectures — Xin, E, Lian, Jian, and Nanjian — and Shaowu Military District had twenty-five sites.
translations.idiomatic: and twenty-five sites in Xin, E, Lian, Jian, and Nanjian prefectures and Shaowu Military District.

sentences.zh: 鉛產越、建、連、英、春、韶、衢、汀、漳、南劍十州，南安、邵武二軍，有三十六場、務。

translations.literal: Lead was produced in ten prefectures — Yue, Jian, Lian, Ying, Chun, Shao, Qu, Ting, Zhang, and Nanjian — and two military districts — Nan'an and Shaowu — with thirty-six sites and bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Lead came from thirty-six sites and bureaus in Yue, Jian, Lian, Ying, Chun, Shao, Qu, Ting, Zhang, and Nanjian prefectures and Nan'an and Shaowu military districts.

sentences.zh: 錫產河南、南康、虔、道、賀、潮、循七州，南安軍，有九場。

translations.literal: Tin was produced in seven prefectures — Henan, Nankang, Qian, Dao, He, Chao, and Xun — and Nan'an Military District, with nine sites.
translations.idiomatic: Tin came from nine sites in Henan, Nankang, Qian, Dao, He, Chao, and Xun prefectures and Nan'an Military District.

sentences.zh: 水銀產秦、階、商、鳳四州，有四場。

translations.literal: Mercury was produced in the four prefectures Qin, Jie, Shang, and Feng, with four sites.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury came from four sites in Qin, Jie, Shang, and Feng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 朱砂產商、宜二州，富順監，有三場。

translations.literal: Cinnabar was produced in the two prefectures Shang and Yi and the Fushun Supervisorate, with three sites.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar came from three sites in Shang and Yi prefectures and the Fushun supervisorate.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，詔曰：「古者不貴難得之貨，後代賦及山澤，上加侵削，下益雕弊。

translations.literal: In Kaibao year 3, an edict said: "In antiquity people did not prize goods hard to obtain; in later ages levies reached mountains and marshes, adding oppression above and increasing exhaustion below.
translations.idiomatic: In 970, an edict declared: "The ancients did not prize rare goods. Later dynasties taxed mountains and marshes, squeezing the top and grinding down the bottom.

sentences.zh: 每念茲事，深疚於懷，未能捐金於山，豈忍奪人之利。

translations.literal: Whenever I think on this matter, I feel deep remorse in my heart; unable to abandon gold in the mountains, how could I bear to seize people's profit?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on this, I feel deep remorse. If I cannot leave gold untouched in the mountains, how can I bear to seize what belongs to the people?

sentences.zh: 自今桂陽監歲輸課銀，宜減三分之一。

translations.literal: From now on the annual silver quota delivered by the Guiyang supervisory office should be reduced by one third.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the annual silver quota of the Guiyang supervisory office shall be cut by one third.

sentences.zh: 」民鑄銅為佛像、浮圖及人物之無用者禁之，銅鐵不得闌出蕃界及化外。

translations.literal: " The people casting copper into Buddha images, pagodas, and useless human figures were forbidden; copper and iron must not pass out through the frontier or beyond the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Private casting of copper into Buddha images, pagodas, and ornamental figures was banned, and copper and iron were forbidden to cross the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，有司言：「定州諸山多銀礦，而鳳州山銅礦復出，采煉大獲，而皆良焉。

translations.literal: In Zhidao year 2, the responsible offices said: "The various mountains of Ding Prefecture contain many silver mines, and copper mines have reappeared in the mountains of Feng Prefecture; smelting has yielded great gains, and all are of fine quality.
translations.idiomatic: In 996, officials reported: "Ding Prefecture's mountains hold rich silver deposits, and copper mines have reopened in Feng Prefecture. Smelting has yielded excellent ore in quantity.

sentences.zh: 請置官署掌其事。

translations.literal: We request establishing an official office to manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that a government office be established to manage production.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「地不愛寶，當與眾庶共之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Taizong said: "The earth does not hoard its treasures; they should be shared with the common people.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizong replied: "The earth does not hoard its treasures — they should be shared with the people.

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: " He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused.

sentences.zh: 東、西川監酒商稅課半輸銀帛外，有司請令二分入金。

translations.literal: Apart from the eastern and western Sichuan wine and merchant-tax levies, half of which were delivered in silver and silk, the responsible offices requested that two tenths be paid in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the eastern and western Sichuan wine and merchant-tax levies, half payable in silver and silk, officials proposed that two tenths be paid in gold.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，詔以非土產罷之。

translations.literal: In Jingde year 3, an edict abolished this because gold was not a local product.
translations.idiomatic: In 1006, an edict abolished the requirement because gold was not a local product.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，登、萊采金，歲益數千兩。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era, gold was mined at Deng and Lai, increasing by several thousand taels a year.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era, gold mining at Deng and Lai yielded several thousand additional taels each year.

sentences.zh: 仁宗命獎勸官吏，宰相王曾曰：「采金多則背本趨末者眾，不宜誘之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong ordered officials rewarded and encouraged; Chancellor Wang Zeng said: "If much gold is mined, many will abandon the root and rush to the branch; it is not fitting to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong ordered rewards for the officials involved. Chancellor Wang Zeng objected: "Heavy gold mining draws people away from farming — we should not encourage it.

sentences.zh: 」景祐中，登、萊饑，詔弛金禁，聽民采取，俟歲豐復故。

translations.literal: " During the Jingyou era, when Deng and Lai suffered famine, an edict relaxed the gold prohibition and allowed the people to mine; when harvests were abundant again, the old rules were restored.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Jingyou era, famine struck Deng and Lai. The court temporarily lifted the gold ban and allowed private mining, restoring the prohibition once harvests recovered.

sentences.zh: 然是時海內承平已久，民間習俗日漸侈靡，糜金以飭服器者不可勝數，重禁莫能止焉。

translations.literal: Yet by this time the realm within the seas had long enjoyed peace; popular customs daily grew more extravagant, and those who squandered gold to adorn clothing and vessels were beyond counting — heavy prohibitions could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: By then the empire had enjoyed peace for generations. Popular taste grew ever more extravagant, and countless people lavished gold on clothing and vessels — no prohibition could check the trend.

sentences.zh: 景祐、慶曆中，屢下詔申敕之，語在《輿服志》。
