translations.literal: During the Jingyou and Qingli eras, edicts were repeatedly issued to reiterate and enforce this; the language is in the "Treatise on Carriages and Apparel."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou and Qingli eras, the court repeatedly issued edicts reinforcing the ban; the full text appears in the Treatise on Carriages and Apparel.

sentences.zh: 大率山澤之利有限，或暴發輒竭，或采取歲久，所得不償其費，而歲課不足，有司必責主者取盈。

translations.literal: Generally, the benefits of mountains and marshes are limited; sometimes sudden discovery is quickly exhausted, or extraction over many years yields gains that do not cover the costs; when the annual quota falls short, the responsible offices invariably require the operators to make up the deficit.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, mountain and marsh resources are finite. Deposits either burst forth and quickly run dry, or yield over years less than they cost to work. When annual quotas fell short, officials invariably pressed mine operators to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 仁宗、英宗每降赦書，輒委所在視冶之不發者，或廢之，或蠲主者所負歲課，率以為常；

translations.literal: Emperors Renzong and Yingzong, whenever they issued amnesty edicts, invariably charged the local authorities to inspect smelteries that were not producing; some were abolished, some had the operators' outstanding annual quotas remitted — this became the usual practice;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperors Renzong and Yingzong issued amnesty edicts, they ordered local authorities to review idle smelteries — closing some, remitting operators' outstanding quotas for others. This became standard practice;

sentences.zh: 而有司有請，亦輒從之，無所吝。

translations.literal: And when the responsible offices made requests, they were likewise invariably granted, without stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: When officials submitted requests of their own, the throne usually granted them without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 故冶之興廢不常，而歲課增損隨之。

translations.literal: Therefore the rise and fall of smelteries was irregular, and increases and decreases in the annual quota followed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Smelteries accordingly rose and fell unpredictably, and annual revenue fluctuated with them.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，歲得金萬五千九十五兩，銀二十一萬九千八百二十九兩，銅五百一十萬八百三十四斤，鐵七百二十四萬一千斤，鉛九萬八千一百五十一斤，錫三十三萬六百九十五斤，水銀二千二百斤。

translations.literal: During the Huangyou era, the annual yield was gold 10,095 taels, silver 219,829 taels, copper 5,100,834 catties, iron 7,241,000 catties, lead 98,151 catties, tin 330,695 catties, and mercury 2,200 catties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era, annual output reached 10,095 taels of gold, 219,829 taels of silver, 5,100,834 catties of copper, 7,241,000 catties of iron, 98,151 catties of lead, 330,695 catties of tin, and 2,200 catties of mercury.

sentences.zh: 其後，以赦書從事或有司所請，廢冶百餘。

translations.literal: Thereafter, acting on amnesty edicts or at the request of responsible offices, more than a hundred smelteries were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently, acting on amnesty orders or official petitions, more than a hundred smelteries were shut down.

sentences.zh: 既而山澤興發，至治平中，或增冶或復故者六十有八，而諸州坑冶總二百七十一：登、萊、商、饒、汀、南恩六州，金之冶十一；

translations.literal: Before long mountains and marshes flourished anew; by the Zhiping era, sixty-eight smelteries were either added or restored to their former state, and the total of mining pits and smelteries in the various prefectures was 271: in the six prefectures of Deng, Lai, Shang, Rao, Ting, and Nan'en, eleven gold smelteries;
translations.idiomatic: Deposits revived in time. By the Zhiping era, sixty-eight smelteries had been added or reopened, bringing the nationwide total to 271 mining and smelting sites: eleven gold works in Deng, Lai, Shang, Rao, Ting, and Nan'en;

sentences.zh: 登、虢、秦、鳳、商、隴、越、衢、饒、信、虔、郴、衡、漳、汀、泉、建、福、南劍、英、韶、連、春二十三州，南安、建昌、邵武三軍，桂陽監，銀之冶八十四；

translations.literal: in the twenty-three prefectures of Deng, Guo, Qin, Feng, Shang, Long, Yue, Qu, Rao, Xin, Qian, Chen, Heng, Zhang, Ting, Quan, Jian, Fu, Nanjian, Ying, Shao, Lian, and Chun, the three military prefectures of Nan'an, Jianchang, and Shaowu, and Guiyang Superintendency, eighty-four silver smelteries;
translations.idiomatic: eighty-four silver works across twenty-three prefectures — Deng, Guo, Qin, Feng, Shang, Long, Yue, Qu, Rao, Xin, Qian, Chen, Heng, Zhang, Ting, Quan, Jian, Fu, Nanjian, Ying, Shao, Lian, and Chun — plus Nan'an, Jianchang, and Shaowu military prefectures and Guiyang Superintendency;

sentences.zh: 饒、信、虔、建、漳、汀、南劍、泉、韶、英、梓十一州，邵武軍，銅之冶四十六；

translations.literal: in the eleven prefectures of Rao, Xin, Qian, Jian, Zhang, Ting, Nanjian, Quan, Shao, Ying, and Zi, and Shaowu Military Prefecture, forty-six copper smelteries;
translations.idiomatic: forty-six copper works in Rao, Xin, Qian, Jian, Zhang, Ting, Nanjian, Quan, Shao, Ying, and Zi prefectures and Shaowu Military Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 登、萊、徐、兗、鳳、翔、陝、儀、邢、虢、磁、虔、吉、袁、信、澧、汀、泉、建、南劍、英、韶、渠、合、資二十四州，興國、邵武二軍，鐵之冶七十七；

translations.literal: in the twenty-four prefectures of Deng, Lai, Xu, Yan, Feng, Xiang, Shan, Yi, Xing, Guo, Ci, Qian, Ji, Yuan, Xin, Li, Ting, Quan, Jian, Nanjian, Ying, Shao, Qu, He, and Zi, and the two military prefectures of Xingguo and Shaowu, seventy-seven iron smelteries;
translations.idiomatic: seventy-seven iron works across twenty-four prefectures — Deng, Lai, Xu, Yan, Feng, Xiang, Shan, Yi, Xing, Guo, Ci, Qian, Ji, Yuan, Xin, Li, Ting, Quan, Jian, Nanjian, Ying, Shao, Qu, He, and Zi — plus Xingguo and Shaowu military prefectures;

sentences.zh: 越、衢、信、汀、南劍、英、韶、春、連九州，邵武軍，鉛之冶三十；

translations.literal: in the nine prefectures of Yue, Qu, Xin, Ting, Nanjian, Ying, Shao, Chun, and Lian, and Shaowu Military Prefecture, thirty lead smelteries;
translations.idiomatic: thirty lead works in Yue, Qu, Xin, Ting, Nanjian, Ying, Shao, Chun, and Lian prefectures and Shaowu Military Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 商、虢、虔、道、賀、潮、循七州，錫之冶十六；

translations.literal: in the seven prefectures of Shang, Guo, Qian, Dao, He, Chao, and Xun, sixteen tin smelteries;
translations.idiomatic: sixteen tin works in Shang, Guo, Qian, Dao, He, Chao, and Xun prefectures;

sentences.zh: 而水銀、丹砂州冶，與至道、天禧之時則一，皆置吏主之。

translations.literal: As for mercury and cinnabar smelteries in the prefectures, they were the same as in the Zhidao and Tianxi eras — officials were appointed in all cases to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural mercury and cinnabar works remained unchanged from the Zhidao and Tianxi eras, each staffed with appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 是歲，視皇祐金減九千六百五十六，銀增九萬五千三百八十四，銅增一百八十七萬，鐵、錫場百餘萬，鉛增二百萬，又得丹砂二千八百餘斤，獨水銀無增損焉。

translations.literal: That year, compared with Huangyou: gold decreased by 9,656; silver increased by 95,384; copper increased by 1,870,000; iron and tin yards by more than 1,000,000; lead increased by 2,000,000; cinnabar gained more than 2,800 catties; mercury alone showed no increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: That year compared with Huangyou, gold fell by 9,656 taels while silver rose by 95,384. Copper rose by 1.87 million catties, iron and tin yards by over a million, and lead by two million. Cinnabar output exceeded 2,800 catties. Only mercury showed no change.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，詔：「天上寶貨坑冶，不發而負歲課者蠲之。

translations.literal: In Xining year 1, an edict said: "For heavenly treasure mining pits and smelteries that do not produce yet owe annual quotas, remit them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1068, an edict declared: "Annual quotas owed by idle imperial treasure mines shall be remitted.

sentences.zh: 」八年，令近坑冶坊郭鄉村並淘采烹煉，人並相為保；

translations.literal: " In year 8, it ordered that urban wards and villages near mining pits and smelteries alike pan, mine, and smelt; people were mutually organized into mutual-responsibility groups;
translations.idiomatic: " In 1075, communities near mines and smelteries were ordered to pan, mine, and smelt collectively, with residents organized into mutual-responsibility groups;

sentences.zh: 保內及於坑冶有犯，知而不糾或停盜不覺者，論如保甲法。

translations.literal: Within a group, or at mining pits and smelteries, if there were offenses and one knew yet did not report, or was negligent and failed to detect theft, punishment followed the mutual-responsibility militia law.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses within a group or at mine sites — whether failing to report known violations or overlooking theft through negligence — were punished under the mutual-responsibility militia law.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，諸坑冶金總收萬七百一十兩，銀二十一萬五千三百八十五兩，銅千四百六十萬五千九百六十九斤，鐵五百五十萬一千九十七斤，鉛九百十九萬七千三百三十五斤，錫二百三十二萬一千八百九十八斤，水銀三千三百五十六斤，朱砂三千六百四十六斤十四兩有奇。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng year 1, from all mining pits the total gold collected was 10,710 taels, silver 215,385 taels, copper 14,605,969 catties, iron 5,501,097 catties, lead 9,197,335 catties, tin 2,321,898 catties, mercury 3,356 catties, and cinnabar 3,646 catties and 14 taels odd.
translations.idiomatic: In 1078, nationwide mine output totaled 10,710 taels of gold, 215,385 taels of silver, 14,605,969 catties of copper, 5,501,097 catties of iron, 9,197,335 catties of lead, 2,321,898 catties of tin, 3,356 catties of mercury, and 3,646 catties and 14 taels of cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 先是，熙寧七年，廣西經略司言：「邕州右江填乃洞產金，請以鄧辟鑒金場。

translations.literal: Previously, in Xining year 7, the Guangxi Frontier Commission said: "At Tian in Yong Prefecture's Right River, Dong people produce gold; we request appointing Deng Pi to oversee a gold field.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in 1074, the Guangxi Frontier Commission reported: "The Tian region on Yong Prefecture's Right River yields gold from Dong territory. We request appointing Deng Pi to establish a gold field there.

sentences.zh: 」後五年，凡得金為錢二十五萬緡，辟遷官者再焉。

translations.literal: " Five years later, the gold obtained in all amounted to 250,000 strings of cash in value; Pi was promoted twice.
translations.idiomatic: " Within five years the field yielded gold worth 250,000 strings of cash, and Pi was promoted twice.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，始以所產薄罷貢，而虔、吉州界鉛悉禁之。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng year 4, because output was slight tribute was first abolished, and lead along the border of Qian and Ji prefectures was entirely prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: In 1081, output proved too thin to sustain tribute payments, and the field was closed. Lead along the Qian–Ji prefectural border was fully banned.

sentences.zh: 七年，戶部尚書王存等請復開銅禁，各展磨勘年有差。

translations.literal: In year 7, Revenue Minister Wang Cun and others requested restoring the copper prohibition; each received an extension of merit-review years by varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1084, Revenue Minister Wang Cun and others petitioned to restore the copper ban and received merit-review extensions of varying length.

sentences.zh: 是歲，坑冶凡一百三十六所，領於虞部。

translations.literal: That year, mining pits and smelteries numbered 136 in all, administered by the Bureau of Parks and Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: That year, 136 mining and smelting sites fell under the Bureau of Parks and Waterways.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，提舉江、淮等路銅事遊經言：「信州膽銅古坑二：一為膽水浸銅，工少利多，其水有限；

translations.literal: In Chongning year 1, the Commissioner for Copper Affairs on the Jianghuai and other circuits, You Jing, said: "Xin Prefecture's ancient vitriol-copper pits are two: one uses vitriol water to leach copper — little labor, much profit, but the water is limited;
translations.idiomatic: In 1102, You Jing, commissioner for copper on the Jianghuai and other circuits, reported: "Xin Prefecture's two ancient vitriol-copper pits differ: leaching copper from vitriol solution requires little labor for great profit, but the water supply is finite;

sentences.zh: 一為膽土煎銅，土無窮而為利寡。

translations.literal: one uses vitriol earth to smelt copper — the earth is inexhaustible but the profit is slight.
translations.idiomatic: smelting from vitriol ore yields an inexhaustible supply but slender profit.

sentences.zh: 計置之初，宜增本損息，浸銅斤以錢五十為本，煎銅以八十。

translations.literal: At the outset of planning, capital should be increased and interest reduced: for leached copper, fifty cash per catty as capital; for smelted copper, eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, capital outlays should be raised and interest charges lowered — fifty cash per catty of leached copper, eighty for smelted.

sentences.zh: 」詔用其言。

translations.literal: " An edict adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The court accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 諸路坑冶，自川、陝、京西之外，並令常平司同管幹。

translations.literal: Mining pits and smelteries on all circuits, apart from Sichuan, Shaanxi, and the Jingxi circuit, were all ordered jointly managed by the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Jingxi, all circuit mines were placed under joint Ever-Normal Granary administration.

sentences.zh: 所收息薄而煩官監者，如元符、紹聖敕立額，許民封狀承買。

translations.literal: Where the profit collected was slight yet official supervision was burdensome, following the quotas established by the Yuanfu and Shaosheng edicts, the people were permitted to submit sealed bids to purchase the franchise.
translations.idiomatic: Sites where profits were thin but official supervision costly could, under Yuanfu and Shaosheng quota rules, be franchised to the highest bidder.

sentences.zh: 四年，湖北旺溪金場，以歲收金千兩，乃置監官。

translations.literal: In year 4, at Wangxi Gold Field in Hubei, because the annual gold yield reached 1,000 taels, a supervising official was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1107, Wangxi Gold Field in Hubei, yielding 1,000 taels annually, received an appointed supervisor.

sentences.zh: 廣東漕臣王覺自言嘗領常平，講求山澤之利，岑水一場去年收銅，比租額增三萬九千一百斤，較之常年亦增六十六萬一千斤。

translations.literal: Guangdong transport commissioner Wang Jue said he had once headed the Ever-Normal Granaries and studied the benefits of mountains and marshes; at one Censhui field last year copper collected exceeded the lease quota by 39,100 catties and, compared with normal years, also increased by 661,000 catties.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong transport commissioner Wang Jue reported that as former head of the Ever-Normal Granaries he had developed mountain and marsh resources: last year Censhui field's copper output exceeded its lease quota by 39,100 catties and surpassed the normal annual yield by 661,000 catties.

sentences.zh: 遂增其秩。

translations.literal: His rank was then increased.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly promoted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，山澤坑冶名數，令監司置籍，非所當收者別籍之，若弛興、廢置、移並，亦令具注，上於虞部。

translations.literal: That year, the registered names and numbers of mountain-and-marsh mining pits and smelteries were ordered recorded in registers by the circuit intendant; those not due for collection were recorded separately; if abandoned, revived, abolished, relocated, or merged, detailed notes were also required and submitted to the Bureau of Parks and Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: That year, circuit intendants were ordered to register all mine and smeltery sites, keeping separate lists for inactive operations, and to note every closure, reopening, relocation, or merger for submission to the Bureau of Parks and Waterways.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，詔：「金銀坑發，雖告言而方檢視，私開淘取者以盜論。

translations.literal: In Daguan year 2, an edict said: "When gold and silver pits are discovered, even if reported and under inspection, those who privately open and pan shall be treated as thieves.
translations.idiomatic: In 1108, an edict declared: "Even after a gold or silver strike is reported and under official inspection, unauthorized mining shall be punished as theft.

sentences.zh: 坑冶舊不隸知縣、縣丞者，並令兼監，賞罰減正官一等。

translations.literal: Mining pits and smelteries not formerly subordinate to the magistrate and assistant magistrate were all ordered placed under their joint supervision; rewards and punishments were one grade below those for regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Mines not previously under magistrate or assistant magistrate supervision were placed under their joint oversight, with rewards and penalties one grade below regular officials.

sentences.zh: 」有冶地，知縣月一行點閱。

translations.literal: " Where there were smeltery sites, the magistrate was to conduct monthly inspection rounds.
translations.idiomatic: " Where smelteries operated, magistrates were required to inspect them monthly.

sentences.zh: 言者論其職在宣導德澤，平征賦獄訟，不宜為課利走山谷間，遂已之。

translations.literal: Critics argued that their duty lay in proclaiming virtue and benevolence and settling taxes, lawsuits, and litigation — it was not fitting to pursue revenue profits rushing through mountain valleys; the policy was therefore dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that magistrates should disseminate imperial benevolence and administer taxes and justice, not chase revenue through mountain valleys — and the order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 八月，提舉陝西坑冶司改並入轉運司。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Commission for Shaanxi Mining and Smelting was reorganized and merged into the Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Shaanxi mining commission was merged into the transport commission.

sentences.zh: 三年，尚書省言：「陝西路坑冶已遣官吏提轄措置，川路金銀坑治興廢，慮失利源。

translations.literal: In year 3, the Department of State Affairs said: "Mining and smelting on the Shaanxi circuit already has dispatched officials to supervise and manage it; the rise and fall of gold and silver pits and smelteries on the Sichuan route is feared to lose revenue sources.
translations.idiomatic: In 1109, the Department of State Affairs warned: "Shaanxi mines are already under special administration, but Sichuan gold and silver operations risk revenue loss through unchecked closures.

sentences.zh: 」詔：「令陝西措置官兼行川路事。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Order the Shaanxi managing official also to handle Sichuan route affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne ordered the Shaanxi mining administrator to take charge of Sichuan operations as well.

sentences.zh: 坑冶所收金、銀、銅、鉛、錫、鐵、水銀、朱砂物數，令工部置籍簽注，歲半消補，上之尚書省。

translations.literal: The quantities of gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, iron, mercury, and cinnabar collected at mining pits and smelteries — order the Ministry of Works to establish registers with annotations; half the year's registers are retired and replenished, and submitted to the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works was ordered to keep annotated registers of all gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, iron, mercury, and cinnabar collected at mines, retiring half each year and forwarding updated records to the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 」自是，戶工部、尚書省皆有籍鉤考，然所憑唯帳狀，至有有額而無收，有收而無額，乃責之縣丞、監官及曹、部奉行者，而更督遞年違負之數。

translations.literal: " From this time, the Revenue and Works ministries and the Department of State Affairs all had registers for audit and examination; yet what they relied on was only ledger forms — so that there were quotas without collection, and collection without quotas; then they held the assistant magistrates, supervising officials, and clerks and ministry executors accountable, and further pressed the accumulated annual deficit figures.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter Revenue, Works, and the Department of State Affairs all maintained audit registers — but relying solely on ledger forms produced quotas without collections and collections without quotas. Assistant magistrates, mine supervisors, and responsible clerks were held liable, then pressed to make up accumulated annual shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 九月，措置陝西坑冶蔣彝奏：本路坑冶收金千六百兩，他物有差。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Jiang Yi, manager of Shaanxi mining and smelting, memorialized: mining pits and smelteries on this circuit collected 1,600 taels of gold; other commodities varied.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Shaanxi mining administrator Jiang Yi reported 1,600 taels of gold and varying amounts of other metals from circuit mines.

sentences.zh: 詔輸大觀西庫，彝增秩，官屬各減磨勘年。

translations.literal: An edict ordered delivery to the Daguan West Treasury; Yi received a rank increase, and each subordinate had merit-review years reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered delivery to the Daguan West Treasury, promoted Jiang Yi, and shortened merit-review periods for his staff.

sentences.zh: 四年，令監司遣官同諸縣丞遍視坑冶之利，為圖籍簽注，監司覆實保奏，議遣官再覆，酌重輕加賞，異同、脫漏者罪之。

translations.literal: In year 4, circuit intendants were ordered to dispatch officials together with all assistant magistrates to survey mining profits throughout, prepare annotated map-registers; circuit intendants verified and memorialized guarantees; consideration was given to dispatching officials for a second verification; rewards were adjusted for weight and importance; those with discrepancies or omissions were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1110, circuit intendants were to send officials with every assistant magistrate to survey mine profitability and prepare annotated maps. Intendants would verify and recommend awards proportional to findings; discrepancies or omissions would be punished after a second review.

sentences.zh: 六年，川、陝路各置提轄措置。

translations.literal: In year 6, Sichuan and Shaanxi circuits each established supervisory management offices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1112, Sichuan and Shaanxi each received dedicated mining administration offices.

sentences.zh: 坑冶官劉芑計置萬、永州產金，一歲收二千四百餘兩，特與增秩。

translations.literal: Mining official Liu Qi, having planned gold production at Wan and Yong prefectures, collected more than 2,400 taels in one year; he was specially granted a rank increase.
translations.idiomatic: Mine administrator Liu Qi, who had developed gold production at Wan and Yong prefectures, yielded over 2,400 taels in a single year and received a special promotion.

sentences.zh: 十二月，廣東漕司言：「本路鐵場坑冶九十二所，歲額收鐵二百八十九萬餘斤，浸銅之餘無他用。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Guangdong Transport Office said: "On this circuit there are ninety-two iron fields and mining smelteries; the annual quota collects more than 2,890,000 catties of iron; apart from leaching copper, there is no other use.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Guangdong's transport office reported: "This circuit's ninety-two iron mines yield over 2.89 million catties annually, with no use beyond copper leaching.

sentences.zh: 」詔令官悉市以廣浸，仍以諸司及常平錢給本。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered officials to purchase it all to expand leaching, and to supply capital from various offices and Ever-Normal Granary funds.
translations.idiomatic: " The court ordered officials to buy it all for expanded leaching operations, funding purchases from departmental and Ever-Normal Granary accounts.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏：「五路坑冶已有提轄措置專司，及淮南、湖北、廣東西亦監司兼領，其餘路請並令監司領之。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs memorialized: "The five circuits' mining pits and smelteries already have dedicated supervisory management offices; Huainan, Hubei, Guangdong, and Guangxi are also jointly overseen by circuit intendants; for the remaining circuits we request that circuit intendants likewise take charge.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs recommended: "Five circuits already have dedicated mining offices; Huainan, Hubei, Guangdong, and Guangxi are jointly managed by circuit intendants — the remaining circuits should follow suit.

sentences.zh: 」於是江東西、福建、兩浙漕臣皆領坑冶。

translations.literal: " Thereupon transport commissioners of Jiangdong-West, Fujian, and the Two Zhe circuits all took charge of mining pits and smelteries.
translations.idiomatic: " Transport commissioners in Jiangdong-West, Fujian, and the Two Zhes accordingly assumed mining oversight.

sentences.zh: 七年，提舉東南九路坑冶徐禋奏：「太平瑞應，史不絕書。

translations.literal: In year 7, Xu Yin, Commissioner for Mining and Smelting on the Southeast Nine Circuits, memorialized: "Auspicious responses in times of great peace — the histories never cease recording them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113, Xu Yin, commissioner for the Southeast Nine Circuits' mines, argued: "Portents of peace fill the historical record without interruption.

sentences.zh: 今部內山澤、坑冶，若獲希世珍物及古寶器，請赴書藝局上進。

translations.literal: Now, within our jurisdiction, from mountains, marshes, and mining pits and smelteries, if rare treasures of the age or ancient precious vessels are obtained, we request sending them up to the Directorate of Books and Arts.
translations.idiomatic: Rare finds from our circuit's mountains, marshes, and mines — extraordinary treasures or antique vessels — should be submitted to the Directorate of Books and Arts.

sentences.zh: 」蓋自政和初，京西漕臣王璹奏太和山產水精，知桂州王覺奏枕門等處產金及生花金田，提轄京西坑冶王景文奏汝州青嶺鎮界產瑪瑙，其後湟州界蕃官結彪地內金坑千餘，收生熟金四等，凡百三十四兩有奇。

translations.literal: " For from the beginning of Zhenghe, Jingxi transport commissioner Wang Dan memorialized that Mount Taihe produced crystal; Gui Prefecture prefect Wang Jue memorialized that Zhenmen and other places produced gold and living-flower gold fields; Jingxi mining commissioner Wang Jingwen memorialized that the Qingling Town boundary of Ru Prefecture produced agate; afterward, within the territory of Fan official Jie Biao on the Huangzhou frontier, more than a thousand gold pits yielded raw and refined gold of four grades, totaling more than 134 taels odd.
translations.idiomatic: " Since early Zhenghe, Jingxi commissioner Wang Dan had reported crystal from Mount Taihe; Gui Prefecture prefect Wang Jue reported gold and "living-flower" gold fields at Zhenmen; Jingxi mining commissioner Wang Jingwen reported agate from Ru Prefecture's Qingling boundary. Later, over a thousand pits in Fan official Jie Biao's Huangzhou territory yielded raw and refined gold of four grades — 134 taels in all.

sentences.zh: 蔡京請宣付史館，帥百官表賀，故禋復有是請焉。

translations.literal: Cai Jing requested announcing it to the Historiography Institute and leading all officials in a congratulatory memorial; therefore Yin again made this request.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing had such finds announced to the Historiography Institute and led officials in congratulatory memorials — hence Yin's petition.

sentences.zh: 是時，河北、京東西及徐禋所領九路興修坑冶，類鑿空擾下，抑州縣承額，於是降黜河北提轄官，遣廉訪使者鄭諶並諸路廉訪悉究陳利病真偽。

translations.literal: At this time, Hebei, Jingdong-West, and the nine circuits under Xu Yin's charge — reopening mining pits and smelteries — generally bored into empty ground to harass subordinates and pressed prefectures and counties to meet quotas; therefore the Hebei mining commissioner was demoted, and integrity censor Zheng Chen together with integrity censors on all circuits were dispatched to thoroughly investigate whether reported benefits and harms were true or false.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei, Jingdong-West, and Yin's nine circuits were reopening mines by fabricating strikes and pressuring local quotas. The Hebei mining commissioner was demoted, and integrity censor Zheng Chen with counterparts on every circuit were dispatched to investigate claimed benefits and abuses.

sentences.zh: 八月，中書奏坑冶浸已即緒，詔京東西、河北路並提舉東南九路坑冶並罷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Secretariat memorialized that mining leaching was already underway; an edict abolished both the Jingdong-West and Hebei mining commissions and the Commissioner for the Southeast Nine Circuits' Mining and Smelting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Secretariat reported leaching operations underway. The court abolished Jingdong-West and Hebei mining commissions and the Southeast Nine Circuits post.

sentences.zh: 十一月，尚書省言：「徐禋以東南黑鉛留給鼓鑄之餘，悉造丹粉，鬻以濟用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Department of State Affairs said: "Xu Yin, reserving southeastern black lead for coin-casting needs, manufactured the remainder into red lead powder and sold it to meet expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the Department reported: "Xu Yin reserved southeastern black lead for coinage and converted the surplus into red lead powder for sale to cover expenses.

sentences.zh: 」詔諸路常平司以三十萬輸大觀西庫，餘從所請。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Ever-Normal Granaries on all circuits to deliver 300,000 to the Daguan West Treasury; the remainder of the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Ever-Normal Granaries on all circuits were ordered to deliver 300,000 strings to the Daguan West Treasury; the rest of Yin's request was approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，令諸路鐵仿茶鹽法榷鬻，置爐冶收鐵，給引召人通市。

translations.literal: The next year, iron on all circuits was ordered sold under monopoly following the tea and salt method: smelting furnaces were established to collect iron; warrants were issued to summon traders for market circulation.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, iron on all circuits was monopolized along tea-and-salt lines: government smelters collected ore and issued permits for licensed trade.

sentences.zh: 苗脈微者聽民出息承買，以所收中賣於官，私相貿易者禁之。

translations.literal: Where ore veins were slight, the people were permitted to advance capital and purchase the franchise; what was collected was sold in part to the government; private mutual trade was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Thin ore veins could be privately franchised with capital advances, with a portion of output sold to the state; private trade was banned.

sentences.zh: 先是，元豐六年，京東漕臣吳居厚奏：「徐、鄆、青等州歲製軍器及上供簡鐵之類數多，而利國、萊蕪二監鐵少不能給。

translations.literal: Previously, in Yuanfeng year 6, Jingdong transport commissioner Wu Ju-hou memorialized: "Xu, Yun, Qing, and other prefectures annually manufacture many military weapons and tribute iron arrowheads and the like, yet the Liguo and Laiwu smelteries produce too little iron to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in 1083, Jingdong commissioner Wu Ju-hou reported: "Xu, Yun, Qing, and neighboring prefectures need large quantities of arms and tribute ironware, but the Liguo and Laiwu smelteries cannot meet demand.

sentences.zh: 請鐵從官興煽，所獲可多數倍。

translations.literal: We request that iron be government-smelted by official operation; what is obtained can be many times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Government smelting, he argued, could multiply output several times over.

sentences.zh: 」自是，官榷鐵造器用以鬻於民，至元祐罷之。

translations.literal: " From this time, the government monopolized iron, forged vessels, and sold them to the people — until the Yuanyou era when it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " The state thereafter monopolized iron, cast goods, and sold them to the public — until the Yuanyou reforms abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 其後大觀初，入內皇城使裴絢為涇原幹當，奏上渭州通判苗衝淑之言：「石河鐵冶既令民自采煉，中賣於官，請禁民私相貿易。

translations.literal: Later, at the beginning of Daguan, Inner Palace envoy Pei Xuan, serving as Jingyuan administrator, memorialized quoting the words of Weizhou vice prefect Miao Chongshu: "At the Shihe Iron Smeltery, since the people are permitted to mine and smelt on their own and sell a portion to the government, we request prohibiting private mutual trade among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Later, early in Daguan, Inner Palace envoy Pei Xuan, Jingyuan administrator, relayed Weizhou vice prefect Miao Chongshu's proposal: "At Shihe Iron Smeltery, where miners smelt privately and sell a portion to the state, private trade among miners should be banned.

sentences.zh: 農具、器用之類，悉官為鑄造，其冶坊已成之物，皆以輸官而償其直。

translations.literal: Agricultural tools, vessels, and the like — all were to be cast by the government; finished goods at the smeltery workshops were all delivered to the government and their price reimbursed.
translations.idiomatic: Farm tools and household wares would be government-cast; finished workshop goods would be surrendered to the state at fair price.

sentences.zh: 」乃禁毋得私相貿易，農具、器用勿禁，官自賣鐵唯許鑄瀉戶市之。

translations.literal: " Private mutual trade was then forbidden; agricultural tools and vessels were not forbidden; government-sold iron was permitted for purchase only by casting shops.
translations.idiomatic: " Private trade was banned — except for farm tools and household wares. Government iron could be sold only to licensed casting shops.

sentences.zh: 政和初，臣僚言：「鹽鐵利均，今鹽筴推行已備，而鐵貨尚未講畫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenghe, officials said: "The profits of salt and iron are equal; now the salt policy is fully implemented, yet iron goods have not yet been planned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenghe, officials argued: "Salt and iron yield equal profit, yet while salt policy is fully enforced, iron commerce remains unregulated.

sentences.zh: 請即冶戶未償之錢，收其已煉之鐵，為器鬻之。

translations.literal: We request taking the outstanding money owed by smelter operators, collecting their already-smelted iron, casting it into vessels, and selling them.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed seizing operators' unpaid debts, taking their smelted iron, casting it into goods, and selling them.

sentences.zh: 兼京東二監所出尤多，河北固鎮等冶並官監，其利不資，而河東鐵、炭最盛，若官榷為器，以贍一路，旁及陝、雍，利入甚廣，且以銷盜鑄之弊。

translations.literal: Moreover, the two Jingdong smelteries produce especially much; Guzhen and other smelteries in Hebei are all under government supervision and their profit is not relied upon; yet iron and coal in Hedong are most abundant — if the government monopolizes casting into vessels to supply one circuit, extending to Shaan and Yong, revenue would be very broad, and moreover it would eliminate the evil of illicit casting.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdong's two smelteries were especially productive; Hebei's Guzhen and other government works needed no subsidy; Hedong's iron and coal were richest of all. A government iron monopoly casting goods for one circuit — extending to Shaan and Yong — would yield broad revenue and curb illicit casting.

sentences.zh: 又夏人茶山鐵冶既入中國，乏鐵為器，聞以鹽易鐵錢於邊，若官自為器，則鐵與錢俱重，可伐其謀。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Tangut Chashan Iron Smeltery having fallen to China, they lack iron for vessels; it is heard they exchange salt for iron cash at the frontier — if the government itself casts vessels, both iron and cash would become heavy, and their scheme could be thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: With the Tangut Chashan smeltery now in Chinese hands, the Tanguts lacked iron for casting and reportedly traded salt for frontier iron coins. Government casting would make both iron and coin scarce, undermining their designs.

sentences.zh: 請榷諸路鐵，擇其最盛者，可置監設官總之，概諸路不越數十處，餘止為鑄瀉之地，屬之都監或監當官兼領。

translations.literal: We request monopolizing iron on all circuits, selecting the most flourishing sites — supervisory offices with officials may be established to oversee them; on all circuits not exceeding several dozen places; the remainder would only serve as casting-shop locations, subordinate to chief supervisors or warehouse managers acting concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed monopolizing iron circuit-wide, establishing supervisory offices at the busiest sites — perhaps several dozen total — with remaining works as casting shops under chief supervisors or warehouse managers.

sentences.zh: 凡農具、器用皆官鑄造，表以字號，官本之餘，取息二分以上，仍置鐵引以通諸路，儲其錢助三路鈔本。

translations.literal: All agricultural tools and vessels would be government-cast, marked with characters and numbers; beyond official capital, interest of two tenths or more would be taken; iron warrants would also be established to circulate through all circuits; the funds stored would assist the paper-note capital of the three circuits.
translations.idiomatic: All farm tools and wares would be government-cast and marked with serial numbers; after recovering capital, interest of twenty percent or more would be charged. Iron trade permits would circulate nationwide, with proceeds supporting paper-note reserves on three circuits.

sentences.zh: 」詔戶部下諸路漕臣詳度。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the Revenue Ministry to send down to transport commissioners on all circuits for detailed assessment.
translations.idiomatic: " The Revenue Ministry was ordered to survey the proposal with transport commissioners on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 會次年，廣東路請以可監之地如舊法收其淨利，苗脈微者召人承買，官不榷取，遂並諸路詳度之旨不行。

translations.literal: The next year coincided with Guangdong Circuit requesting that supervisable sites, following the old method, collect net profit; where ore veins were slight, people were summoned to purchase the franchise, with no government monopoly — thus the order for detailed assessment on all circuits was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Guangdong petitioned to collect net profits at supervised sites under the old method, franchising thin veins without state monopoly — and the nationwide assessment was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 至是，臣僚復以為言，故嚴貿易之禁，而鐵利盡榷於官，然農具、器用從民鑄造，卒如舊法。

translations.literal: At this point, officials again raised the matter; therefore trade prohibitions were tightened, and iron profits were entirely monopolized by the government; yet agricultural tools and vessels were permitted to be cast by the people, ultimately following the old method.
translations.idiomatic: Officials raised the matter again, tightening trade restrictions and fully monopolizing iron profits — though farm tools and wares remained privately cast, as before.

sentences.zh: 四月，廣東廉訪黃烈等言：「廣、惠、英、康、韶州、興慶府，政和中，寶貨司立坑冶金銀等歲額，或苗脈微，或無人承買，而浮冗之人虛托其名，發毀民田，騷動邀販。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Guangdong integrity censor Huang Lie and others said: "Guang, Hui, Ying, Kang, Shao prefectures and Xingqing Prefecture — during Zhenghe, the Treasure Bureau established annual quotas for mining gold, silver, and the like; sometimes ore veins were slight, sometimes no one purchased the franchise, yet idle and redundant persons falsely used others' names, opened and destroyed private fields, causing disturbance and extorting sales.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Guangdong censor Huang Lie reported: "During Zhenghe, the Treasure Bureau set annual gold and silver quotas for Guang, Hui, Ying, Kang, Shao, and Xingqing — but thin veins and absent bidders let idle opportunists claim franchises in others' names, ravaging farmland and extorting locals.

sentences.zh: 」詔：「政和六年所立額並罷，舊有苗脈可給歲課者如故。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "The quotas established in Zhenghe year 6 are all abolished; where old ore veins can still meet the annual levy, the former practice remains.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenghe 6 quotas were abolished; viable old veins would continue under former levy arrangements.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，復諸路元罷提舉坑冶官，其江南路仍令江西漕臣劉蒙同措置。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month, the formerly abolished Commissioners for Mining and Smelting on all circuits were restored; for Jiangnan Circuit, Jiangxi transport commissioner Liu Meng was still ordered to manage jointly.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month, abolished circuit mining commissioners were restored; Jiangnan operations remained jointly managed by Jiangxi commissioner Liu Meng.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，石泉軍江溪沙磧麩金，許民隨金脈淘采，立課額，或以分數取之。

translations.literal: In Xuanhe year 1, at Shiquan Military Prefecture's Jiang Stream sandbars yielding placer gold, the people were permitted to pan along gold veins; a levy quota was established, or a fractional share was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In 1119, placer gold at Shiquan Military Prefecture's Jiang Stream sandbars was opened to licensed panning along gold veins, with levies set as fixed quotas or fractional shares.

sentences.zh: 十月，復置相州安陽縣銅冶村監官。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the supervising official at Tongye Village Smeltery in Anyang County, Xiang Prefecture, was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the supervisor at Xiang Prefecture's Anyang County Tongye Village copper works was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔留邢州綦村、磁州固鎮兩冶，餘創置冶並罷，而常平司謂銅冶村近在河北，得利多，故有是命。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict retained the two smelteries of Qicun in Xing Prefecture and Guzhen in Ci Prefecture, abolishing all newly established smelteries; yet the Ever-Normal Granaries held that Tongye Village was near Hebei and profit was great — hence this order.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had kept only Xing Prefecture's Qicun and Ci Prefecture's Guzhen smelteries, closing all others — but the Ever-Normal Granaries noted Tongye Village's proximity to Hebei and strong profits, prompting reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔：「坑冶之利，二廣為最，比歲所入，稽之熙、豐，十不逮一。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict said: "The profit of mining pits and smelteries — the Two Guangs are greatest; annual intake compared with the Xining and Yuanfeng eras does not reach one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, an edict lamented: "Mining profits were richest in the Two Guangs, yet recent revenue barely matched one-tenth of Xining–Yuanfeng levels.

sentences.zh: 令漕臣鄭良提舉經畫，分任官屬典掌計置，取元豐以來歲入多數立額，定為常賦，坑冶司毋預焉。

translations.literal: Order transport commissioner Zheng Liang to supervise planning, assigning subordinates to manage arrangements; take the highest annual intakes since Yuanfeng to establish quotas, fixing them as regular levies — the Mining Bureau is not to intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Zheng Liang was charged with restructuring operations, setting permanent quotas based on peak Yuanfeng-era yields — without mining bureau involvement.

sentences.zh: 」時江、淮、荊、浙等九路，坑冶凡二百四十五，鑄錢院監十八，歲額三百餘萬緡。

translations.literal: " At this time, on the nine circuits of Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, and others, mining pits and smelteries numbered 245 in all, coin-casting directorate supervisors 18, annual quota more than 3,000,000 strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time, nine circuits including Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe operated 245 mines, 18 coin-casting offices, and annual quotas exceeding three million strings.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔：「坑冶舊隸轉運司者，如熙、豐、紹聖法；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict said: "Mining pits and smelteries formerly subordinate to the Transport Commission — follow the Xining, Yuanfeng, and Shaosheng methods;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, an edict restored Xining–Yuanfeng–Shaosheng rules for mines formerly under transport commissions;

sentences.zh: 崇寧以後隸常平司者，如崇寧法；

translations.literal: those subordinate to the Ever-Normal Granaries after Chongning — follow the Chongning method;
translations.idiomatic: Chongning rules for mines placed under Ever-Normal Granaries after that era;

sentences.zh: 其江、淮等路坑冶官屬，如熙、豐員數，餘路官屬並罷，仍令中書選提點官。」

translations.literal: for mining official posts on the Jiang, Huai, and other circuits — follow the Xining and Yuanfeng staffing numbers; official posts on remaining circuits are all abolished; still order the Secretariat to select intendant officials."
translations.idiomatic: Jianghuai circuit staffing would match Xining–Yuanfeng levels; other circuits' mining posts were abolished; the Secretariat would appoint circuit intendants."

sentences.zh: 南渡，坑冶廢興不常，歲入多寡不同。

translations.literal: After the Southern Crossing, the rise and fall of mining pits and smelteries was irregular, and annual intake varied in amount.
translations.idiomatic: After the Southern Crossing, mines rose and fell unpredictably, and annual revenue fluctuated widely.

sentences.zh: 今以紹興三十二年金、銀、銅、鐵、鉛、錫之冶廢興之數一千一百七十，及乾道二年鑄錢司比較所入之數附之：

translations.literal: Now, appended herewith are the 1,170 figures for the rise and fall of gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin smelteries in Shaoxing year 32, and the comparative intake figures of the Coin-Casting Office in Qiandao year 2:
translations.idiomatic: Below are appended 1,170 records of gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin smelteries' status in 1162, plus comparative revenue figures from the Coin-Casting Office in 1166:

sentences.zh: 湖南、廣東、江東西金冶二百六十七，廢者一百四十二；

translations.literal: gold smelteries in Hunan, Guangdong, and Jiangdong-West — 267; abolished — 142;
translations.idiomatic: Hunan, Guangdong, and Jiangdong-West gold works: 267 total, 142 closed;

sentences.zh: 湖南、廣東、福建、浙東、廣西、江東西銀冶一百七十四，廢者八十四；

translations.literal: silver smelteries in Hunan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhedong, Guangxi, and Jiangdong-West — 174; abolished — 84;
translations.idiomatic: Hunan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhedong, Guangxi, and Jiangdong-West silver works: 174 total, 84 closed;

sentences.zh: 潼川、湖南、利州、廣東、浙東、廣西、江東西、福建銅冶一百九，廢者四十五。

translations.literal: copper smelteries in Tongchuan, Hunan, Lizhou, Guangdong, Zhedong, Guangxi, Jiangdong-West, and Fujian — 109; abolished — 45.
translations.idiomatic: Tongchuan, Hunan, Lizhou, Guangdong, Zhedong, Guangxi, Jiangdong-West, and Fujian copper works: 109 total, 45 closed.

sentences.zh: 舊額歲七百五萬七千二百六十斤有奇，乾道歲入二十六萬三千一百六十斤有奇。

translations.literal: old quota — annually 7,507,260 catties odd; Qiandao annual intake — 263,160 catties odd.
translations.idiomatic: Former quota: 7,507,260 catties annually; Qiandao intake: 263,160 catties.

sentences.zh: 淮西、夔州、成都、利州、廣東、福建、浙東、廣西、江東西鐵冶六百三十八，廢者二百五十一，舊額歲二百一十六萬二千一百四十斤有奇，乾道歲入八十八萬三百斤有奇。

translations.literal: iron smelteries in Huai West, Kuizhou, Chengdu, Lizhou, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhedong, Guangxi, and Jiangdong-West — 638; abolished — 251; old quota — annually 2,162,140 catties odd; Qiandao annual intake — 880,300 catties odd.
translations.idiomatic: Huai West, Kuizhou, Chengdu, Lizhou, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhedong, Guangxi, and Jiangdong-West iron works: 638 total, 251 closed; former quota 2,162,140 catties, Qiandao intake 880,300 catties.

sentences.zh: 淮西、湖南、廣東、福建、浙東、江西鉛冶五十二，廢者一十五，舊額歲三百二十一萬三千六百二十斤有奇，乾道歲入一十九萬一千二百四十斤有奇。

translations.literal: lead smelteries in Huai West, Hunan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhedong, and Jiangxi — 52; abolished — 15; old quota — annually 3,213,620 catties odd; Qiandao annual intake — 191,240 catties odd.
translations.idiomatic: Huai West, Hunan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhedong, and Jiangxi lead works: 52 total, 15 closed; former quota 3,213,620 catties, Qiandao intake 191,240 catties.

sentences.zh: 湖南、廣東、江西錫冶一百一十八，廢者四十四，舊額歲七十六萬一千二百斤有奇，乾道歲入二萬四百五十斤有奇。

translations.literal: tin smelteries in Hunan, Guangdong, and Jiangxi — 118; abolished — 44; old quota — annually 761,200 catties odd; Qiandao annual intake — 20,450 catties odd.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan, Guangdong, and Jiangxi tin works: 118 total, 44 closed; former quota 761,200 catties, Qiandao intake 20,450 catties.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年，宰執言：「封樁銀數比淳熙末年虧額幾百五十萬。

translations.literal: In Qingyuan year 2, the chief counselors said: "The sealed-reserve silver count, compared with the end of the Chunxi era, falls short by nearly 1,500,000.
translations.idiomatic: In 1196, chief counselors reported: "Sealed silver reserves have fallen nearly 1.5 million short of late Chunxi levels.

sentences.zh: 今務場所入歲不滿三十萬，而歲奉三宮及冊寶費約四十萬，恐愈侵銀額。

translations.literal: Now the annual intake of the exchange bureaus does not reach 300,000, yet annual expenses for the Three Palaces and seal-and-tablet ceremonies are about 400,000 — it is feared the silver quota will be further encroached upon.
translations.idiomatic: Exchange bureau revenue now falls below 300,000 annually, while ceremonies for the Three Palaces and imperial regalia cost some 400,000 — threatening further erosion of silver reserves.

sentences.zh: 欲權以三分為率，一分支銀，二分支會子。

translations.literal: It was proposed provisionally to take one-third as the ratio: one part disbursed in silver, two parts in huizi.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed a provisional rule of thirds: one third paid in silver, two thirds in paper notes (huizi).

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Very well."

sentences.zh: 端平三年，赦曰：「諸路州縣坑冶興廢，在觀寺、祠廟、公宇、居民墳地及近墳園林地者，在法不許人告，亦不得受理。

translations.literal: In Duanping year 3, an amnesty said: "In all circuits, prefectures, and counties, the establishment or abandonment of mines and smelteries located at monasteries, temples, shrines, public offices, residential grave lands, and nearby grave groves and forest lands — by law people may not report these, nor may [officials] accept such cases.
translations.idiomatic: In 1235 an amnesty decreed: "Where mines and smelteries were opened or closed on monastery, temple, shrine, or government grounds, on residential burial plots, or on grave groves and woodlands nearby, the law forbade private denunciations — and officials were forbidden to accept such cases.

sentences.zh: 訪聞官司利於告發，更不究實，多致擾害。

translations.literal: It was reported that officials profited from encouraging denunciations, no longer investigated the facts, and caused much harassment and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were said to encourage denunciations for profit without verifying facts, causing widespread abuse.

sentences.zh: 自今許人戶越訴，官吏並訟者重置典憲。

translations.literal: From now on households are permitted to lodge direct appeals; officials and litigants alike shall be severely punished according to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Households were henceforth allowed to appeal directly to higher authority; officials and plaintiffs alike would face severe statutory penalties.

sentences.zh: 及有坑冶停閉、苗脈不發之所，州縣勒令坑戶虛認歲額，提點鑄錢司核實追正。」

translations.literal: And where mines and smelteries had been stopped or closed and ore veins did not yield, prefectures and counties forced mine operators to falsely acknowledge annual quotas; the Commissioner for Minting was to verify the facts and correct them."
translations.idiomatic: Where closed mines or exhausted veins led prefectures to force operators to report false quotas, the Commissioner for Minting was ordered to verify the figures and set them right."

sentences.zh: 礬唐於晉州置平陽院以收其利。

translations.literal: Alum: In Tang, the Pingyang Office was established at Jin Prefecture to collect its profit.
translations.idiomatic: Alum — under Tang, Jin Prefecture established the Pingyang Office to capture alum revenues.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，度支奏罷之，乃以礬山歸之州縣。

translations.literal: In Kaicheng year 3, the Revenue Department memorialized to abolish it, and the alum mountains were returned to the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In 838 the Revenue Department petitioned to abolish the office, and alum hills reverted to local prefectural control.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，復創務置官吏，宋因之。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties onward, the office was re-established with officials placed; Song followed this practice.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Dynasties onward the monopoly was revived with appointed officials; the Song kept the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 白礬出晉、慈、坊州、無為軍及汾州之靈石縣，綠礬出慈、隰州及池州之銅陵縣，皆設官典領，有鑊戶鬻造入官市。

translations.literal: White alum came from Jin, Ci, and Fang Prefectures, Wuwei Army, and Lingshi County in Fen Prefecture; green alum came from Ci and Xi Prefectures and Tongling County in Chi Prefecture. In all cases officials were appointed to oversee; cauldron households brewed and sold to the government market.
translations.idiomatic: White alum came from Jin, Ci, and Fang prefectures, Wuwei Army, and Lingshi County in Fenzhou; green alum from Ci and Xi prefectures and Tongling in Chizhou. Each region had supervising officials; licensed cauldron households brewed alum for the state market.

sentences.zh: 晉、汾、慈州礬，以一百四十斤為一馱，給錢六十。

translations.literal: Alum from Jin, Fen, and Ci Prefectures: one load was reckoned at one hundred forty jin, and sixty strings of cash were paid.
translations.idiomatic: For alum from Jin, Fen, and Ci, one load equaled 140 jin and paid 60 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 隰州礬馱減三十斤，給錢八百。

translations.literal: The Xi Prefecture alum load was reduced by thirty jin, and eight hundred strings of cash were paid.
translations.idiomatic: In Xi Prefecture the load was 110 jin, with a payment of 800 strings.

sentences.zh: 博賣白礬價：晉州每馱二十一貫五百，慈州又增一貫五百；

translations.literal: Bulk-sale price for white alum: Jin Prefecture, twenty-one strings five hundred cash per load; Ci Prefecture added another one string five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Bulk-sale prices for white alum: Jin Prefecture charged 21,500 cash per load; Ci Prefecture added another 1,500;

sentences.zh: 綠礬：汾州每馱二十四貫五百，慈州又增五百，隰州每馱四貫六百。

translations.literal: Green alum: Fen Prefecture, twenty-four strings five hundred cash per load; Ci Prefecture added another five hundred; Xi Prefecture, four strings six hundred cash per load.
translations.idiomatic: Green alum: Fenzhou 24,500 cash per load; Cizhou added 500; Xizhou 4,600 per load.

sentences.zh: 散賣白礬：坊州斤八十錢，汾州百九十二錢，無為軍六十錢；

translations.literal: Retail sale of white alum: Fang Prefecture, eighty cash per jin; Fen Prefecture, one hundred ninety-two cash; Wuwei Army, sixty cash;
translations.idiomatic: Retail white alum sold for 80 cash per jin in Fangzhou, 192 in Fenzhou, and 60 in Wuwei Army;

sentences.zh: 綠礬，斤七十錢。

translations.literal: Green alum: seventy cash per jin.
translations.idiomatic: Green alum sold for 70 cash per jin.

sentences.zh: 先是，建隆二年，命左諫議大夫劉熙古詣晉州製置礬，許商人輸金銀、布帛、絲綿、茶及緡錢，官償以礬，凡歲增課八十萬貫。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Jianlong year 2, Left Remonstrance Grandee Liu Xigu was ordered to go to Jin Prefecture to organize alum production; merchants were permitted to deliver gold, silver, cloth, silk, cotton, tea, and strings of cash, and the government repaid them in alum; in all, annual revenue increased by eight hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in 961, Left Remonstrance Grandee Liu Xigu was sent to Jin Prefecture to reorganize the alum monopoly. Merchants could deliver gold, silver, cloth, silk, cotton, tea, or cash and receive alum in return; annual revenue rose by 800,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，歲博緡錢、金銀計一十二萬餘貫，茶計三萬餘貫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era, annual exchange in strings of cash and gold and silver totaled more than one hundred twenty thousand strings; tea totaled more than thirty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era, annual barter brought in more than 120,000 strings in cash, gold, and silver, and more than 30,000 strings' worth of tea.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，銀、絹帛二萬餘貫，茶計十四萬貫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duan Gong era, silver and silk totaled more than twenty thousand strings; tea totaled one hundred forty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duan Gong era, silver and silk amounted to more than 20,000 strings, and tea to 140,000.

sentences.zh: 」至是，言者謂：「礬直酬以見錢，商人以陳茶入博，有利豪商，無資國用。

translations.literal: " By then, critics said: "Alum should be paid for in ready cash, yet merchants barter with stale tea — this benefits wealthy merchants and does not support state revenue.
translations.idiomatic: By then critics argued: "Alum ought to be paid for in ready cash, but merchants were bartering with stale tea — enriching powerful traders while doing nothing for the treasury.

sentences.zh: 」詔今後惟聽金銀、見錢入博。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that henceforth only gold, silver, and ready cash would be accepted for barter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict limited future barter to gold, silver, and ready cash alone.

sentences.zh: 至道中，白礬歲課九十七萬六千斤，綠礬四十萬五千餘斤，鬻錢一十七萬餘貫。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era, white alum annual quota was nine hundred seventy-six thousand jin; green alum, more than four hundred five thousand jin; sale revenue, more than one hundred seventy thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era, white alum yielded 976,000 jin a year, green alum more than 405,000 jin, and sales revenue exceeded 170,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 真宗末，白礬增二十萬一千餘斤，綠礬增二萬三千餘斤，鬻錢增六萬九千餘貫。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Zhenzong's reign, white alum increased by more than two hundred one thousand jin; green alum by more than twenty-three thousand jin; sale revenue by more than sixty-nine thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Zhenzong's reign, white alum had risen by more than 201,000 jin, green alum by more than 23,000 jin, and sales revenue by more than 69,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 天聖以來，晉、慈二州礬募民鬻之，季鬻礬一盆，多者千五、六百斤，少者六、七百斤，四分輸一入官，餘則官市之。

translations.literal: Since the Tiansheng era, alum in Jin and Ci Prefectures recruited the people to sell it; each quarter one basin of alum was sold — at most one thousand five or six hundred jin, at least six or seven hundred jin; one quarter was delivered to the government, and the remainder was purchased by the government market.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tiansheng era onward, Jin and Ci recruited households to sell alum quarterly. Each batch filled one basin — as much as 1,500–1,600 jin or as little as 600–700. One quarter went to the state; the rest was bought at the official market.

sentences.zh: 無為軍亦置務鬻礬，後聽民自鬻，官置場售之，私售礬禁如私售茶法。

translations.literal: Wuwei Army also established an office to sell alum; later the people were permitted to sell it themselves, with the government setting up a market to sell it; private sale of alum was forbidden under the same rules as private sale of tea.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei Army likewise established an alum monopoly office; later households were allowed to brew alum themselves while the state ran sales depots. Private alum sales were banned under the same penalties as illicit tea.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔弛兩蜀榷礬之禁。

translations.literal: In year 6, an edict relaxed the alum monopoly prohibition in the Two Shu regions.
translations.idiomatic: In 1028 an edict lifted the alum monopoly in both Shu circuits.

sentences.zh: 時河東礬積益多，復聽入金帛、芻粟。

translations.literal: At the time Hedong alum stockpiles grew ever larger, and payment in gold, silk, and fodder grain was again permitted.
translations.idiomatic: As Hedong alum stockpiles mounted, the state again accepted gold, silk, and fodder grain in payment.

sentences.zh: 芻粟虛估高，商人利於入中。

translations.literal: Fodder and grain were overvalued in assessment, and merchants profited from delivering goods in kind.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder and grain were assessed at inflated values, so merchants profited from delivering goods in kind.

sentences.zh: 麟州粟鬥實直錢百，虛估增至三百六十，礬之出官為錢二萬一千五百，才易粟六石，計粟實直錢才六千，而礬一馱已費本錢六十。

translations.literal: At Lin Prefecture grain's actual value per dou was one hundred cash, but the assessed value was raised to three hundred sixty; alum leaving official stores was priced at twenty-one thousand five hundred cash, yet exchanged for only six shi of grain; calculating the grain's actual value at only six thousand cash, while one load of alum had already cost sixty strings in capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Lin Prefecture grain worth 100 cash per dou was assessed at 360. Alum leaving official stores was priced at 21,500 cash yet bought only six shi of grain — worth a mere 6,000 cash at market rates — while each load had already cost the state 60 strings in capital.

sentences.zh: 縣官徒有榷礬之名，其實無利。

translations.literal: The government had only the name of an alum monopoly; in reality there was no profit.
translations.idiomatic: The state held the monopoly in name only; in practice it made no profit.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，罷入芻粟，復令入緡錢。

translations.literal: In Jiayou year 6, payment in fodder and grain was abolished, and payment in strings of cash was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1061 payment in fodder and grain was abolished and cash payment restored.

sentences.zh: 礬以百四斤為一馱，入錢京師榷貨務者，為錢十萬七千；

translations.literal: Alum was reckoned one hundred four jin to a load; payment at the Capital Monopoly Bureau was one hundred seven thousand cash;
translations.idiomatic: Alum was reckoned at 104 jin per load; payment at the Capital Monopoly Bureau was 107,000 cash;

sentences.zh: 入錢麟、府州者，又減三千。

translations.literal: Payment at Lin and Fu Prefectures was further reduced by three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: payment at Lin and Fu prefectures was reduced by another 3,000.

sentences.zh: 自是商賈不得專其利矣。

translations.literal: From this time merchants could no longer monopolize the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants could no longer capture the profit for themselves.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，晉、慈入礬二百二十七萬三千八百斤，以易芻粟之類，為緡錢十三萬六千六百；

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era, Jin and Ci delivered two million two hundred seventy-three thousand eight hundred jin of alum, exchanged for fodder, grain, and the like, yielding one hundred thirty-six thousand six hundred strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Jin and Ci delivered 2,273,800 jin of alum, exchanged for fodder and grain worth 136,600 strings;

sentences.zh: 無為軍礬售緡錢三萬三千一百。

translations.literal: Wuwei Army alum sales yielded thirty-three thousand one hundred strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei Army alum sales brought in 33,100 strings.

sentences.zh: 治平中，晉、慈礬損一百九萬六千五百四斤；

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era, Jin and Ci alum fell by one million ninety-six thousand five hundred four jin;
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiping, Jin and Ci alum deliveries fell by 1,096,504 jin;

sentences.zh: 無為軍礬售錢歲有常課，發運使領之，視皇祐數無增損；

translations.literal: Wuwei Army alum sales had a fixed annual quota, overseen by the transport commissioner; compared with the Huangyou figures there was neither increase nor decrease;
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei Army maintained a fixed annual alum quota under the transport commissioner, unchanged from Huangyou levels;

sentences.zh: 隰州礬至是入三十九萬六千斤，亦以易緡錢助河東歲糴。

translations.literal: Xi Prefecture alum at this time delivered three hundred ninety-six thousand jin, likewise exchanged for strings of cash to assist Hedong's annual grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Prefecture now delivered 396,000 jin, likewise exchanged for cash to subsidize Hedong's annual grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，命河東轉運司經畫礬、鹽遺利。

translations.literal: In Xining year 1, the Hedong Transport Commission was ordered to plan remaining profits from alum and salt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1068 the Hedong transport commission was ordered to recover untapped alum and salt revenues.

sentences.zh: 李師中言：「官積礬三百斤，走鹵消耗，恐後為棄物。

translations.literal: Li Shizhong said: "The government stockpile of three hundred jin of alum loses salt to efflorescence and consumption; I fear it will later become waste.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhong warned: "Three hundred jin of alum in government stores was efflorescing and losing salt; it risked becoming worthless scrap.

sentences.zh: 」詔令商人入中糧草，即以償之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that merchants delivering grain and fodder in kind be repaid with it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed merchants who delivered grain and fodder to be paid in alum.

sentences.zh: 三年，罷潞州交子務，以妨中納糧草、算請礬鹽故也。

translations.literal: In year 3, the Luzhou Jiaozi Office was abolished because it hindered delivery of grain and fodder in kind and bidding for alum and salt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070 the Luzhou jiaozi office was abolished because it interfered with grain deliveries and competitive bidding for alum and salt.

sentences.zh: 知慶州王廣淵言：「河東，礬為利源之最，請河東、京東、河北、陝西別立礬法，專置提舉官。

translations.literal: Wang Guangyuan, prefect of Qing Prefecture, said: "In Hedong, alum is the foremost source of profit. I request that separate alum laws be established for Hedong, Jingdong, Hebei, and Shaanxi, with dedicated intendant officials.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Prefecture prefect Wang Guangyuan argued: "In Hedong, alum is the richest revenue source. He asked that Hedong, Jingdong, Hebei, and Shaanxi each receive a separate alum code with dedicated intendant officials.

sentences.zh: 」詔遣光祿丞楊蟠會議以聞。

translations.literal: " An edict dispatched Palace Provisioner Yang Pan to confer and report.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Palace Provisioner Yang Pan to consult on the proposal and report back.

sentences.zh: 蟠言：「坊州產礬，官雖置場，而商多私售。

translations.literal: Yang Pan said: "Fang Prefecture produces alum; although the government has set up a market, merchants mostly sell privately.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pan reported: "Fangzhou produces alum, and though the state ran official markets, merchants sold mostly on the black market.

sentences.zh: 請置鑊戶，定其數，許於陝西北界黃河，東限潼關，南及京西、均、房、襄、鄧、金州、光化軍，令鑊戶遞相保察。

translations.literal: I request that cauldron households be established and their numbers fixed; they are permitted from the Yellow River on Shaanxi's northern border, east to Tong Pass, south to Jingxi, Jun, Fang, Xiang, Deng, Jin Prefecture, and Guanghua Army; the cauldron households are to keep watch on one another.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed licensing cauldron households within fixed quotas, bounded on the north by the Yellow River in Shaanxi, on the east by Tong Pass, and on the south by Jingxi, Jun, Fang, Xiang, Deng, Jin Prefecture, and Guanghua Army — with households bound to mutual surveillance.

sentences.zh: 或私賣越界，禁如私白礬法，仍增官獲私礬輒以夾雜減斤重之法。

translations.literal: If anyone sells privately across the boundary, the prohibition follows the law on private white alum; moreover, when officials seize private alum they are to apply the rule on adulteration that reduces weight.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-border private sales would be punished like illicit white alum; officials seizing contraband could further reduce weight for adulteration, as under existing white-alum law.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧初，礬法始變。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the Xining era, the alum law began to change.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening of the Xining reforms, alum policy began to change.

sentences.zh: 歲課所入，元年為錢三萬六千四百緡有奇，並增者五年，乃取熙寧六年中數，定以十八萬三千一百緡有奇為新額；

translations.literal: Annual revenue intake in the first year was thirty-six thousand four hundred odd strings of cash; after five years of continuous increase, the median figure for Xining year 6 was taken and a new quota fixed at one hundred eighty-three thousand one hundred odd strings;
translations.idiomatic: First-year revenue was 36,400-odd strings; after five years of growth the median for 1073 was taken and a new quota of 183,100-odd strings was set;

sentences.zh: 至元豐六年，課增至三十三萬七千九百緡，而無為軍礬歲課一百五十萬斤，用本錢萬八千緡；

translations.literal: By Yuanfeng year 6, revenue had risen to three hundred thirty-seven thousand nine hundred strings; Wuwei Army alum annual quota was one million five hundred thousand jin, requiring capital of eighteen thousand strings;
translations.idiomatic: By 1083 revenue reached 337,900 strings; Wuwei Army's annual quota was 1.5 million jin, requiring capital of 18,000 strings;

sentences.zh: 自治平至元豐數無增損。

translations.literal: From Zhiping to Yuanfeng the figures showed neither increase nor decrease.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhiping through Yuanfeng those figures held steady.

sentences.zh: 初，熙、豐間，東南九路官自賣礬，發運司總之。

translations.literal: Initially, during the Xi and Feng eras, the government in the southeast nine circuits sold alum itself, overseen by the transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, under the Xi and Feng reforms, the southeast's nine circuits sold alum directly under transport commission oversight.

sentences.zh: 元祐初通商，紹聖復熙、豐之制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou commerce was opened; in Shaosheng the Xi and Feng system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou briefly opened alum to private trade; Shaosheng restored the Xi-Feng system.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，定河北、河東礬額各二十四萬緡，淮南九萬緡，罷官賣，從商販，而河東、河北、淮南各置提舉官。

translations.literal: In Daguan year 1, alum quotas for Hebei and Hedong were fixed at two hundred forty thousand strings each and Huainan at ninety thousand strings; official sale was abolished and merchant trade permitted; Hedong, Hebei, and Huainan each received intendant officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1107 quotas were set at 240,000 strings each for Hebei and Hedong and 90,000 for Huainan; official sales ended and merchant trade was allowed, with new intendants in Hedong, Hebei, and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 政和初，復官鬻，罷商販如舊制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenghe, official sale was restored and merchant trade abolished, as under the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenghe official sales resumed and private trade was abolished, restoring the earlier monopoly.

sentences.zh: 淮南礬事司罷歸發運司，上供礬錢責以三萬三千一百緡為額。

translations.literal: The Huainan Alum Affairs Office was abolished and returned to the transport commission; tribute alum revenue was fixed at a quota of thirty-three thousand one hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan's alum affairs office was dissolved and its work returned to the transport commission, with a tribute quota of 33,100 strings.

sentences.zh: 三年，有司奏減河北、河東並淮南礬額，計十六萬緡。

translations.literal: In year 3, the relevant offices memorialized to reduce alum quotas in Hebei, Hedong, and Huainan, totaling one hundred sixty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 officials petitioned to cut Hebei, Hedong, and Huainan quotas by a combined 160,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 四年，礬額復循大觀之制。

translations.literal: In year 4, alum quotas again followed the Daguan system.
translations.idiomatic: In 1114 quotas were restored to Daguan levels.

sentences.zh: 五年，河北、河東綠礬聽客販於東南九路，民間見用者，依通商地籍之，聽買新引帶賣，大率循仿鹽法。

translations.literal: In year 5, green alum from Hebei and Hedong was permitted to be sold by merchants in the southeast nine circuits; what the people currently used was registered according to open-trade territory rules; purchase of new permits and resale were permitted — broadly following the salt law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1115 green alum from Hebei and Hedong could be sold by licensed merchants in the southeast's nine circuits. Household stocks were registered as under open-trade rules; new permits allowed resale — broadly mirroring salt policy.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，舉比較增虧賞罰，未幾，以擾民罷。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era, comparison of surplus and deficit for rewards and punishments was instituted; before long it was abolished for harassing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanhe, surplus-and-deficit comparisons tied to rewards and penalties were introduced but soon abolished for harassing the populace.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，措置財用黃潛厚奏許商人販淮南礬入東南諸路，聽輸錢行在，而持引據赴場支礬。

translations.literal: In Jianyan year 3, Huang Qianhou, commissioner for arranging finances, memorialized permitting merchants to sell Huainan alum into the various circuits of the southeast; they were permitted to pay money at the temporary capital and, holding permits, go to the depot to receive alum.
translations.idiomatic: In 1129 finance commissioner Huang Qianhou petitioned to let merchants sell Huainan alum in the southeast circuits, pay at the court in exile, and collect alum at depots with official permits.

sentences.zh: 紹興十一年，以鑄錢司韓球言，撫州青膽礬斤錢一百二十文，土礬斤三十文省，鉛山場所產品高於撫，青膽礬斤作一百五十文，黃礬斤作八十文。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing year 11, on the memorial of Han Qiu of the Minting Office: Qingdan alum in Fu Prefecture was one hundred twenty cash per jin; native alum, thirty cash per jin; products from the Qianshan depot were superior to Fu's — Qingdan alum was set at one hundred fifty cash per jin, and yellow alum at eighty cash per jin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1141, following Han Qiu of the minting office, prices were set at 120 cash per jin for Qingdan alum in Fuzhou and 30 for native alum; Qianshan's superior product commanded 150 cash for Qingdan alum and 80 for yellow alum.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以淮西提舉司言，取紹興二十四年至二十八年所收礬錢一年中數四萬一千五百八十五緡為定額。

translations.literal: In year 29, on the memorial of the Huai West Intendant's Office, the median annual alum revenue from Shaoxing years 24 through 28 — forty-one thousand five hundred eighty-five strings — was taken as the fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: In 1159 the Huai West intendant's office fixed the quota at 41,585 strings, the median annual alum revenue from 1154–1158.

sentences.zh: 其他產礬之所，若潭州瀏陽之永興場、韶州之岑水場，皆置場給引，歲有常輸。

translations.literal: Other alum-producing places, such as Yongxing Depot in Liuyang, Tan Prefecture, and Censhui Depot in Shao Prefecture, all established depots issuing permits, with fixed annual deliveries.
translations.idiomatic: Other alum districts — Yongxing Depot in Liuyang, Tanzhou, and Censhui Depot in Shaozhou — likewise ran licensed depots with fixed annual deliveries.

sentences.zh: 惟漳州之東，去海甚邇，大山深阻，雖有采礬之利，而潮、梅、汀、贛四州之奸民聚焉，其魁傑者號大洞主、小洞主，土著與負販者，皆盜賊也。

translations.literal: Only east of Zhang Prefecture, very near the sea, in deep and rugged mountains — although there was profit in mining alum — wicked people from the four prefectures of Chao, Mei, Ting, and Gan gathered there; their leaders were called Great Cave Lords and Lesser Cave Lords; natives and peddlers alike were bandits.
translations.idiomatic: East of Zhangzhou alone, close to the coast in steep mountain country, alum could be mined — but outlaws from Chao, Mei, Ting, and Gan prefectures congregated there. Their chiefs styled themselves Great and Lesser Cave Lords; locals and itinerant traders alike were bandits.

sentences.zh: 香宋之經費，茶、鹽、礬之外，惟香之為利博，故以官為市焉。

translations.literal: Incense: among Song state revenues, apart from tea, salt, and alum, only incense yielded broad profit; therefore the government made it a state market.
translations.idiomatic: Incense — after tea, salt, and alum, incense offered the broadest margins among Song monopolies, and so the state kept it under official control.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，泉州抽買乳香一十三等，八萬六千七百八十斤有奇。

translations.literal: In Jianyan year 4, Quanzhou compulsorily purchased frankincense in thirteen grades, totaling eighty-six thousand seven hundred eighty odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1130 Quanzhou compulsorily purchased 86,780-odd jin of frankincense across thirteen grades.

sentences.zh: 詔取赴榷貨務打套給賣，陸路以三千斤、水路以一萬斤為一綱。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it sent to the Monopoly Bureau to be bundled and sold; overland convoys were three thousand jin each, and water convoys ten thousand jin each.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the stock to the Monopoly Bureau for bundling and sale — 3,000 jin per overland convoy and 10,000 jin per river convoy.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，郴、桂寇起，以科買乳香為言。

translations.literal: In Chunxi year 2, bandits rose in Chen and Gui, citing forced purchase of frankincense as their grievance.
translations.idiomatic: In 1175 bandits rose in Chen and Gui prefectures, protesting forced frankincense purchases.

sentences.zh: 詔：「湖南路見有乳香並輸行在榷貨務，免科降。

translations.literal: An edict said: "All frankincense currently held in Hunan Circuit is to be sent to the Monopoly Bureau at the temporary capital, exempt from forced requisition.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "All frankincense held in Hunan Circuit was to be sent to the Monopoly Bureau at the court in exile, exempt from forced requisition.

sentences.zh: 」十二年，分撥榷貨務乳香於諸路給賣，每及一萬貫，輸送左藏南庫。

translations.literal: " In year 12, frankincense from the Monopoly Bureau was allocated to the various circuits for sale; whenever ten thousand strings were reached, it was sent to the South Vault of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In 1185 Monopoly Bureau frankincense was allocated to circuits for retail sale; every 10,000 strings realized was remitted to the Left Treasury's South Vault.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以諸路分賣乳香擾民，令止就榷貨務招客算請。

translations.literal: In year 15, because circuit distribution of frankincense for sale harassed the people, it was ordered that sales be limited to inviting merchants to bid at the Monopoly Bureau alone.
translations.idiomatic: In 1188 circuit distribution was deemed abusive; sales were restricted to competitive bidding at the Monopoly Bureau alone.

sentences.zh: 紹熙三年，以福建舶司乳香虧數，詔依前博買。

translations.literal: In Shaoxi year 3, because the Fujian Maritime Trade Office showed a shortfall in frankincense, an edict ordered a return to competitive purchase as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1192, with Fujian's maritime trade office falling short on frankincense deliveries, the court restored competitive purchasing.

sentences.zh: 開禧三年，住博買。

translations.literal: In Kaixi year 3, competitive purchase was halted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1207 competitive purchasing was halted.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十二年，臣僚言以金銀博買，泄之遠夷為可惜，乃命有司止以絹帛、錦錡、瓷漆之屬博易。

translations.literal: In Jiading year 12, court officials memorialized that using gold and silver for competitive purchase and leaking it to distant barbarians was regrettable; the relevant offices were therefore ordered to barter only with silk, brocade, porcelain, lacquerware, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In 1219 officials argued that paying gold and silver for frankincense leaked precious metal to foreign traders; the court limited barter to silk, brocade, porcelain, lacquerware, and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 聽其來之多寡，若不至則任之，不必以為重也。

translations.literal: They were to accept however much arrived; if it did not come, let it be — it need not be treated as vital.
translations.idiomatic: Imports would be accepted in whatever quantity arrived; shortfalls were to be tolerated — frankincense need no longer be treated as indispensable.
